l122.s2: p thumb, i index, m middle and a ring. The letters come from their Spanish names: pulgar, índice, medio, anular.
l122.s3: The thumb plays the basses: E, A and D. Listen.
l122.s4: "Keep your thumb a little ahead of the other fingers, as if it drew an X with your index."
l122.c1b: The picking-hand fingers are named with letters: p thumb, i index, m middle and a ring. The little finger is hardly used.
l122.c2b: The thumb plucks downward with the side of its tip, ahead of the other fingers. Listen to the open basses.
l122.c3b: To start: p on the basses (6th, 5th and 4th), i on the 3rd, m on the 2nd and a on the 1st.
l122.q1: Which letter is the middle finger?
l122.q2: Which strings does the thumb play in a simple arpeggio?
l122.pads: Tap the buttons in order p, i, m, a, one per beat.
l122.play: With your thumb, play the open basses that light up, in time.

l123.title: The fretting hand
l123.objective: Fret with the tips of fingers 1 to 4, one finger per fret, and play them on the 1st string at 60 bpm.
l123.s1: "Now the other hand. Its fingers are numbered: 1 index, 2 middle, 3 ring and 4 little finger."
l123.s2: One finger per fret: finger 1 on fret 1, finger 2 on fret 2, and so on.
l123.s3: Press with the tip, just behind the fret wire. Listen to all four on the 1st string.
l123.s4: "Don't squeeze too hard: just enough for the note to ring clean."
l123.c1b: Look at the drawing: each finger has its own fret. That way your hand doesn't jump and you reach every note.
l123.c2b: F, F♯, G and G♯ on the 1st string, and back.
l123.c3b: Your fretting thumb sits behind the neck, roughly opposite finger 2. The classical neck is wide: don't grab it with your whole hand.
l123.q1: Where do you press the string?
l123.q1o1: With the fingertip, just behind the fret wire
l123.q1o2: On top of the fret wire
l123.tap: On the fretboard, press frets 1, 2, 3 and 4 on the 1st string.
l123.play: One finger per fret on the 1st string: 1, 2, 3, 4 and back, in time.

l124.title: Your tone: the fingertip
l124.objective: Pluck with the flesh of the fingertip for a round tone, tell it from nail tone, and alternate i-m on the 1st string in time.
l124.s1: "Listen to the same string played in two different ways."
l124.s2: With the flesh of the fingertip: a round, soft tone.
l124.s3: With the nail: brighter and louder.
l124.s4: "In this course we play with the fingertips. What matters now is alternating: i, m, i, m."
l124.c1b: In this course you play with the flesh of the fingertip, the soft pad at the tip. It gives a warm, round tone, and you don't need to look after nails.
l124.c2b: Some players use long, filed nails: louder and clearer. You don't need them: you can play the whole course with your fingertips. Keep your picking-hand nails short.
l124.c3b: Never pluck twice in a row with the same finger: i, m, i, m… as if you were walking.
l124.ear: Listen. Is it played with flesh or with nail?
l124.pads: Alternate i and m, one tap per beat.
l124.play: Alternate i-m on the open 1st string, in time.

l125.title: Your first arpeggio
l125.objective: Play a p-i-m-a arpeggio on open strings at 60 bpm without skipping notes.
l125.s1: "Let's put it all together: the thumb on the basses and the other three fingers on the trebles."
l125.s2: An arpeggio is the notes of a chord played one at a time.
l125.s3: p on the bass, then i, m and a. Listen.
l125.s4: "Now faster, at 70. It already sounds like a classical guitar!"
l125.c1b: Playing the notes of a chord one at a time instead of together. It's the basis of classical guitar accompaniment: zamba, bossa and ballads.
l125.c2b: In each bar, the thumb plays a bass (6th, 5th or 4th), then i, m and a play the 3rd, 2nd and 1st. Listen at 60 bpm.
l125.c3b: Don't mute the strings: in an arpeggio the notes blend and sound like a chord.
l125.q1: In this arpeggio, which finger plays the bass note of each bar?
l125.pads: Tap p, i, m, a in order, one tap per beat.
l125.play: Play the arpeggio: p on the bass that lights up, then i, m and a on the 3rd, 2nd and 1st.

l131.title: Free stroke with i-m
l131.objective: Pluck with free strokes, alternating i-m on the 1st and 2nd strings at 70 bpm.
l131.s1: "There are two ways to pluck with your fingers. Today, the first one: the free stroke."
l131.s2: The finger plucks the string with its tip and follows through toward the palm, without touching the next string.
l131.s3: Alternate i and m on the 1st and the 2nd. Listen.
l131.s4: "With free strokes the other strings keep ringing: perfect for arpeggios."
l131.c1b: The fingertip catches the string and moves up toward the palm. The neighboring strings keep ringing.
l131.c2b: Four times on the 1st, four on the 2nd, then two and two. Never twice in a row with the same finger.
l131.q1: After a free stroke, what does the finger do?
l131.q1o1: It moves toward the palm without touching another string
l131.q1o2: It rests on the next string
l131.q1o3: It mutes the string it played
l131.pads: Alternate i and m, one tap per beat.
l131.play: Free strokes, alternating i-m: open 1st and 2nd strings, in time.

l132.title: Rest stroke with i-m
l132.objective: Use rest strokes to make a melody stand out, and play a melody on the 1st and 2nd strings at 70 bpm.
l132.s1: "The second way: the rest stroke. It sounds louder and fuller."
l132.s2: The finger plucks the string and comes to rest on the next one, the lower string.
l132.s3: A melody on the 2nd and 1st strings: B, C, D, E, F and G. Listen.
l132.s4: "Rest strokes for melodies; free strokes for arpeggios."
l132.c1b: The finger goes through the string and stops on the next, lower one. That string doesn't sound: the finger just rests there.
l132.c2b: Notes on the 2nd string (open, frets 1 and 3) and the 1st (open, frets 1 and 3). Listen and follow the tab.
l132.c3b: Rest strokes when you want a note to stand out, like a melody. Free strokes when the strings have to keep ringing together.
l132.q1: You play the 1st string with a rest stroke. Where does the finger end up?
l132.q1o1: In the air, toward the palm
l132.q2: What are rest strokes good for?
l132.play: With rest strokes, alternating i-m, play the melody that lights up.

l133.title: Changing strings
l133.objective: Keep alternating i-m while moving between strings (3rd, 2nd and 1st) at 70 bpm.
l133.s1: "Playing one string isn't the hard part: it's jumping to another without losing the alternation."
l133.s2: G, B, E, B: the hand stays still and only the fingers move.
l133.s3: "If you stumble, slow down. Clean first, fast later."
l133.s4: Keep the pulse steady when you change strings.
l133.c1b: 3rd, 2nd, 1st and 2nd, over and over, alternating i-m. Listen at 70 bpm.
l133.c2b: Don't move your wrist to reach each string: the fingers get there on their own. The thumb can rest on the 6th.
l133.q1: You played the 3rd string with i. The next note is on the 2nd. Which finger do you use?
l133.tap: Tap these open strings on the fretboard: 3rd, 2nd, 1st and 2nd.
l133.play: Alternating i-m, play open 3rd, 2nd, 1st, 2nd… in time.

l134.title: Thumb on the basses
l134.objective: Play a bass line with your thumb on the 6th, 5th and 4th strings at 70 bpm.
l134.s1: "The thumb is the bass player of the classical guitar."
l134.s2: It plucks downward with the side of the tip, then rests on the string below or moves out.
l134.s3: A line that goes up and down: E, G, A, B, D, E. Listen.
l134.s4: "Keep the thumb ahead of the fingers so they don't collide."
l134.c1b: The thumb pushes the string down, toward the floor. Keep it straight and ahead of i, m and a.
l134.c2b: Open strings and frets 2 and 3 on the 6th, 5th and 4th. Listen and follow the tab.
l134.q1: Which way does the thumb push the string?
l134.ear: Listen to three notes. Do they go up or down?
l134.play: With your thumb, play the bass line that lights up, in time.

l135.title: Thumb + i-m
l135.objective: Combine the thumb on a bass with i-m on the trebles in a p-i-m-i pattern at 70 bpm.
l135.s1: "Now both at once: the thumb plays the bass and the fingers play the rest."
l135.s2: p on a bass, i on the 3rd, m on the 2nd and i again on the 3rd.
l135.c1b: The thumb plays open E, A or D on beat 1. Then i, m, i on the 3rd and 2nd strings.
l135.c2b: Four bars: only the bass changes. The fingers repeat the same thing.
l135.pads: Tap p, i and m in order, one tap per beat.
l135.play: Play the pattern: p on the bass that lights up, then i, m, i.

l141.title: Just behind the fret
l141.objective: Press with the fingertip just behind the fret wire so the note rings clean, with no buzz.
l141.s1: "Is your note buzzing? It's almost always where you press."
l141.s2: The finger goes just before the fret wire, on the nut side, with the tip.
l141.s3: Notes on frets 1 and 3 of the 2nd and 1st strings. Listen.
l141.s4: "Keep your fretting-hand nails short, or you can't press with the tip."
l141.c1b: Press close to the fret wire, not in the middle of the space. You need less force and the note rings clean.
l141.c2b: C and D on the 2nd string; F and G on the 1st. Listen to the melody.
l141.q1: A note buzzes. What do you change first?
l141.q1o1: Move the finger closer to the fret wire
l141.play: Play the notes that light up, with your fingertip just behind the fret.

l142.title: One finger per fret
l142.objective: Play 1-2-3-4 and 4-3-2-1 on the 6th and 1st strings, one finger per fret, at 70 bpm.
l142.s1: "Four fingers, four frets. Each one in its place."
l142.s2: Index on 1, middle on 2, ring on 3 and little finger on 4.
l142.s3: Up and down on the 6th. Listen.
l142.s4: "Keep your fingers close to the strings even when you're not using them."
l142.c1b: Each finger lives on its fret. Going up, leave the ones you used down; going back, lift only the one that's done.
l142.c2b: 1-2-3-4 and 4-3-2-1 on the 6th, then the same on the 1st. Listen.
l142.tap: On the fretboard, press frets 1, 2, 3 and 4 on the 6th string.
l142.play: One finger per fret: 1-2-3-4 and back, on the 6th and the 1st.

l143.title: Chromatic on 6 strings
l143.objective: Play the 1-2-3-4 chromatic on all 6 strings, up and down, cleanly at 70 bpm.
l143.s1: "The exercise every guitarist uses to warm up."
l143.s2: 1-2-3-4 on the 6th, then the 5th, all the way to the 1st. Then back.
l143.s3: "Your picking hand keeps alternating i-m the whole time."
l143.s4: Slow and clean. Speed comes on its own.
l143.c1b: The three bass strings, four notes each. One finger per fret and i-m alternating.
l143.c2b: A few minutes a day is enough. If your hand gets tired, stop and shake it out.
l143.q1: During the chromatic, what does the picking hand do?
l143.play: Chromatic 1-2-3-4 on all 6 strings, up and down, in time.

l144.title: Neighboring strings
l144.objective: Move the chromatic from one string to the next without a gap, on three pairs of strings.
l144.s1: "The tricky moment: when finger 4 is done and finger 1 has to go to another string."
l144.s2: Up the 2nd, on along the 1st, back down the 1st and finish on the 2nd.
l144.s3: "Move finger 1 right as the last note rings, not before."
l144.c1b: 1-2-3-4 on the 2nd, 1-2-3-4 on the 1st, and back 4-3-2-1. Listen.
l144.c2b: While the last note on one string rings, already look at where the next finger goes.
l144.tap: On the fretboard: 1-2-3-4 on the 4th, on the 3rd, and back.
l144.play: Chromatic there and back on the two strings that light up, in time.

l145.title: Stopping notes
l145.objective: Stop a fretted note by relaxing the finger without lifting it off the string, to respect the rests.
l145.s1: "A rest is played too: you have to stop the note on time."
l145.s2: Relax the finger without lifting it: the string stops ringing.
l145.s4: "If you lift the finger all the way, the open string rings. Just relax!"
l145.c1b: The finger keeps touching the string but stops pressing. The note stops without the open string ringing.
l145.c2b: Each note lasts one beat and each rest another. Listen with the metronome.
l145.ear: Listen. Does the note keep ringing or stop?
l145.play: Play the notes and stop them on each rest, in time.

l151.title: The pulse
l151.objective: Keep a steady pulse at 70 bpm, with and without the metronome.
l151.s1: "Music has a heart that beats evenly: the pulse."
l151.s2: The metronome marks the pulse with a click. Play it with your thumb on the 6th.
l151.s3: "When the click stops, keep going on your own without rushing."
l151.s4: An even pulse: not faster, not slower.
l151.c1b: Eight thumb strokes on the open 6th, together with the click.
l151.c2b: Count 1, 2, 3, 4 while you play. 1 is the start of each bar.
l151.pulse: Tap the screen on each beat. Halfway, the click stops: keep going.
l151.play: With your thumb, play the open 6th on each beat.

l152.title: Whole, half and quarter notes
l152.objective: Play notes lasting 4, 2 and 1 beats from tab, in time.
l152.s2: A quarter note lasts one beat, a half note two and a whole note four.
l152.s3: Listen to a bar with all three.
l152.s4: "Let each note ring until the end of its length."
l152.c1b: Two quarter notes, a half note and a whole note on the 1st. Count the beats while you listen.
l152.c2b: In the app's tab, longer notes are drawn longer. Listen to four bars on open strings.
l152.q1: How many beats does a half note last?
l152.tab: Read the tab and tap each note on the fretboard.
l152.play: Play each note for its full length, in time.

l153.title: Eighth notes
l153.objective: Play eighth notes (two per beat) and rests, alternating i-m at 60 bpm.
l153.s1: "What if you have to play faster than the pulse? Eighth notes."
l153.s2: Two eighth notes fit in one beat: "1 and, 2 and".
l153.s3: Listen to eighths and quarters mixed.
l153.s4: "With i-m alternating, eighth notes come out even."
l153.c1b: Count "1 and 2 and": eighth notes fall on the number and on the "and".
l153.c2b: Four bars with eighths, quarters and rests. Listen with the metronome.
l153.tap: Alternate i and m, two taps per beat.
l153.play: Play the melody with eighth notes and rests, in time.

l154.title: Reading tab
l154.objective: Read a 4-bar tab with fretted notes and play it at 70 bpm.
l154.s1: "Tab is a map: each line is a string and each number is a fret."
l154.s2: The top line is the 1st string, the highest. The bottom one is the 6th.
l154.c1b: Six lines, one per string: the 1st on top and the 6th at the bottom. The number tells you which fret to press.
l154.c2b: Notes on the 3rd, 2nd and 1st strings, with fingers 1, 2 and 3.
l154.q1: In tab, which string is the top line?
l154.tab: Read the tab and tap each note on the fretboard.

l155.title: Sight-reading
l155.objective: Read and play a new tab without hearing it first.
l155.s1: "No example today: you read and you play."
l155.s2: Look at the whole tab before you start: strings, frets and lengths.
l155.s3: "Find where each finger goes before you play."
l155.s4: Slow and without stopping: if you slip, keep going.
l155.c1b: Check which strings it uses, which frets and which notes are longer. Count the beats in each bar.
l155.c2b: If you make a mistake, go on to the next note. Keeping the pulse matters more than never missing.
l155.tab: Read the new tab and tap each note on the fretboard.
l155.play: Play the new tab, in time, without stopping.

cp1.intro: Show what you learned in level 1: ear, reading, pulse, the chromatic and a melody with eighth notes.
cp1.ear: You'll hear the open 6th string and then another open string. Which one is it?
cp1.tab: Read this new tab and tap each note on the fretboard.
cp1.pulse: Keep the pulse at 80 bpm. Halfway, the click stops.
cp1.spider: Chromatic 1-2-3-4 on all 6 strings, up and down, alternating i-m.
cp1.melody: Play the melody with eighth notes and rests at 80 bpm, alternating i-m.

l211.title: E minor (Em)
l211.objective: Fret E minor (Em), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l211.s1: "A new chord for the album: E minor (Em)."
l211.s2: Finger 2 on fret 2 of the 5th string and finger 3 on fret 2 of the 4th. All 6 strings ring.
l211.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l211.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l211.c1b: Finger 2 on fret 2 of the 5th string and finger 3 on fret 2 of the 4th. All 6 strings ring. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l211.c2b: Just two fingers: the easiest chord to start with. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l211.tap: Press the notes of E minor (Em) on the fretboard.
l211.arp: Fret E minor (Em) and play string by string, from low to high.
l211.strum: Strum E minor (Em) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l212.title: A minor (Am)
l212.objective: Fret A minor (Am), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l212.s1: "A new chord for the album: A minor (Am)."
l212.s2: Finger 1 on fret 1 of the 2nd string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 4th and finger 3 on fret 2 of the 3rd. Don't play the 6th.
l212.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l212.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l212.c1b: Finger 1 on fret 1 of the 2nd string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 4th and finger 3 on fret 2 of the 3rd. Don't play the 6th. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l212.c2b: Your thumb starts on the 5th string, A: the note that names the chord. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l212.tap: Press the notes of A minor (Am) on the fretboard.
l212.arp: Fret A minor (Am) and play string by string, from low to high.
l212.strum: Strum A minor (Am) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l213.title: E major (E)
l213.objective: Fret E major (E), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l213.s1: "A new chord for the album: E major (E)."
l213.s2: Like Em, plus finger 1 on fret 1 of the 3rd string. All 6 strings ring.
l213.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l213.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l213.c1b: Like Em, plus finger 1 on fret 1 of the 3rd string. All 6 strings ring. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l213.c2b: One finger turns the chord from sad to bright: minor to major. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l213.tap: Press the notes of E major (E) on the fretboard.
l213.arp: Fret E major (E) and play string by string, from low to high.
l213.strum: Strum E major (E) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l214.title: A major (A)
l214.objective: Fret A major (A), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l214.s1: "A new chord for the album: A major (A)."
l214.s2: Fingers 1, 2 and 3 on fret 2 of the 4th, 3rd and 2nd strings. Don't play the 6th.
l214.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l214.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l214.c1b: Fingers 1, 2 and 3 on fret 2 of the 4th, 3rd and 2nd strings. Don't play the 6th. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l214.c2b: Three fingers on the same fret: squeeze them together, the classical neck is wide. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l214.tap: Press the notes of A major (A) on the fretboard.
l214.arp: Fret A major (A) and play string by string, from low to high.
l214.strum: Strum A major (A) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l215.title: D major (D)
l215.objective: Fret D major (D), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l215.s1: "A new chord for the album: D major (D)."
l215.s2: Finger 1 on fret 2 of the 3rd string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 1st and finger 3 on fret 3 of the 2nd. Play the 4th to the 1st.
l215.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l215.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l215.c1b: Finger 1 on fret 2 of the 3rd string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 1st and finger 3 on fret 3 of the 2nd. Play the 4th to the 1st. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l215.c2b: A triangle of fingers on the treble strings. The thumb starts on the 4th, D. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l215.tap: Press the notes of D major (D) on the fretboard.
l215.arp: Fret D major (D) and play string by string, from low to high.
l215.strum: Strum D major (D) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l221.title: C major (C)
l221.objective: Fret C major (C), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l221.s1: "A new chord for the album: C major (C)."
l221.s2: Finger 3 on fret 3 of the 5th string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 4th and finger 1 on fret 1 of the 2nd. Don't play the 6th.
l221.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l221.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l221.c1b: Finger 3 on fret 3 of the 5th string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 4th and finger 1 on fret 1 of the 2nd. Don't play the 6th. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l221.c2b: A staircase of fingers. Arch them so the open 3rd and 1st strings ring. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l221.tap: Press the notes of C major (C) on the fretboard.
l221.arp: Fret C major (C) and play string by string, from low to high.
l221.strum: Strum C major (C) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l222.title: G major (G)
l222.objective: Fret G major (G), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l222.s1: "A new chord for the album: G major (G)."
l222.s2: Finger 2 on fret 3 of the 6th string, finger 1 on fret 2 of the 5th and finger 3 on fret 3 of the 1st. All 6 ring.
l222.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l222.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l222.c1b: Finger 2 on fret 3 of the 6th string, finger 1 on fret 2 of the 5th and finger 3 on fret 3 of the 1st. All 6 ring. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l222.c2b: The fingers sit far apart: open your hand wide. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l222.tap: Press the notes of G major (G) on the fretboard.
l222.arp: Fret G major (G) and play string by string, from low to high.
l222.strum: Strum G major (G) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l223.title: D minor (Dm)
l223.objective: Fret D minor (Dm), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l223.s1: "A new chord for the album: D minor (Dm)."
l223.s2: Finger 1 on fret 1 of the 1st string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd and finger 3 on fret 3 of the 2nd. Play the 4th to the 1st.
l223.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l223.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l223.c1b: Finger 1 on fret 1 of the 1st string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd and finger 3 on fret 3 of the 2nd. Play the 4th to the 1st. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l223.c2b: Compare it with D: only the 1st string changes, and it sounds sad. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l223.tap: Press the notes of D minor (Dm) on the fretboard.
l223.arp: Fret D minor (Dm) and play string by string, from low to high.
l223.strum: Strum D minor (Dm) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l224.title: E seventh (E7)
l224.objective: Fret E seventh (E7), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l224.s1: "A new chord for the album: E seventh (E7)."
l224.s2: Like E without finger 3: finger 2 on fret 2 of the 5th string and finger 1 on fret 1 of the 3rd. All 6 ring.
l224.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l224.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l224.c1b: Like E without finger 3: finger 2 on fret 2 of the 5th string and finger 1 on fret 1 of the 3rd. All 6 ring. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l224.c2b: The seventh adds tension: the chord "wants" to resolve to Am or A. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l224.tap: Press the notes of E seventh (E7) on the fretboard.
l224.arp: Fret E seventh (E7) and play string by string, from low to high.
l224.strum: Strum E seventh (E7) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l225.title: A seventh (A7)
l225.objective: Fret A seventh (A7), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l225.s1: "A new chord for the album: A seventh (A7)."
l225.s2: Finger 2 on fret 2 of the 4th string and finger 3 on fret 2 of the 2nd; the open 3rd rings. Don't play the 6th.
l225.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l225.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l225.c1b: Finger 2 on fret 2 of the 4th string and finger 3 on fret 2 of the 2nd; the open 3rd rings. Don't play the 6th. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l225.c2b: It's the blues chord: you'll use it a lot in level 3. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l225.tap: Press the notes of A seventh (A7) on the fretboard.
l225.arp: Fret A seventh (A7) and play string by string, from low to high.
l225.strum: Strum A seventh (A7) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l231.title: The guide finger
l231.objective: Change between Em and Em7, and between Am and Am7, moving only one finger and keeping the pulse.
l231.s1: "Some changes are almost free: one finger stays and another moves."
l231.s2: Em7: finger 2 on fret 2 of the 5th string and finger 3 on fret 3 of the 2nd; the open 4th rings.
l231.s3: Am7 is Am lifting finger 3: the 3rd string rings open.
l231.s4: "The finger that doesn't move is your guide finger."
l231.c1b: Two new chords for the album: Em7 and Am7. Listen to all four, two beats each.
l231.c2b: The same with your fingers. Notice which finger stays still on each change.
l231.tap: Press the notes of Em7 on the fretboard.
l231.arp: Fret Am7 and play string by string.
l231.strum: Strum Em, Em7, Am and Am7 in half notes, in time.
l231.pimi: Play Em, Em7, Am and Am7 in p-i-m-i, in time.

l232.title: Fingers as a block
l232.objective: Change between E and Am moving all three fingers together, as a block.
l232.s1: "Look at E and Am: it's the same shape!"
l232.s2: Move E's three fingers down one string and you get Am.
l232.s3: Move the whole hand without breaking the shape.
l232.s4: "First in the air, then on the strings."
l232.c1b: E and Am use the same finger positions, one string apart. Listen to the change in half notes.
l232.c2b: Change on beat 1 of each bar. The thumb moves from the 6th string to the 5th.
l232.q1: You fret E and move all three fingers one string down (toward the floor). Which chord do you get?
l232.strum: Strum E and Am in half notes, in time.
l232.pimi: Play E and Am in p-i-m-i, in time.

l233.title: Changing early
l233.objective: Add D7 and G7, and change chords by releasing your hand on the last beat of the bar.
l233.s1: "The trick of fast changers: they get there a little early."
l233.s2: D7: finger 1 on fret 1 of the 2nd string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd and finger 3 on fret 2 of the 1st.
l233.s3: G7: finger 3 on fret 3 of the 6th string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 5th and finger 1 on fret 1 of the 1st.
l233.s4: "On beat 4 you can already let go: an open string rings and nobody notices."
l233.c1b: Two new chords for the album: D7 and G7. Listen to all four, in quarter notes.
l233.c2b: On the last beat of each bar, your hand is already heading to the next chord.
l233.tap: Press the notes of G7 on the fretboard.
l233.arp: Fret D7 and play string by string.
l233.strum: Strum D, D7, G and G7 in quarter notes, in time.
l233.pimi: Play D, D7, G and G7 in p-i-m-i, in time.

l234.title: One-minute changes
l234.objective: Repeat hard changes (C and G, Em and Am, D and A) without losing the pulse.
l234.s1: "Hard changes are practiced on their own, over and over."
l234.s2: C and G: finger 3 moves from the 5th string to the 1st.
l234.s3: Start slow. Once it's clean, raise the tempo.
l234.s4: "One minute per pair, every day. It works!"
l234.c1b: The hardest change in this part. Listen, in quarter notes.
l234.c2b: The thumb moves from the 5th string (C) to the 6th (G).
l234.strum1: Strum Em and Am in quarter notes, in time.
l234.strum2: Strum D and A in quarter notes, in time.
l234.strum: Strum C and G in quarter notes, in time.
l234.pimi: Play C and G in p-i-m-i, in time.

l235.title: 4-chord progressions
l235.objective: Link 4 chords in a row, strummed and in p-i-m-i, in time.
l235.s1: "Four chords in a row: that's how songs sound."
l235.s2: G, Em7, Am7 and D7: it sounds like a song.
l235.s3: And Am, Dm, E7 and Am: it sounds like a zamba or a tango.
l235.s4: "With this you can already accompany songs from the songbook."
l235.c1b: One bar per chord, strummed in quarter notes. Listen.
l235.c2b: The same progression with your fingers.
l235.strum1: Strum Am, Dm, E7 and Am in quarter notes, in time.
l235.strum: Strum G, Em7, Am7 and D7 in quarter notes, in time.
l235.pimi: Play G, Em7, Am7 and D7 in p-i-m-i, in time.

l241.title: Quarter notes with the thumb
l241.objective: Strum downward with your thumb, one stroke per beat, at 70 bpm.
l241.s1: "On the classical guitar you strum with your fingers. The first strum: the thumb."
l241.s2: The thumb falls from the 6th string to the 1st, gently, with the fingertip.
l241.s4: "Count out loud and change chords on 1."
l241.c1b: Keep your wrist loose and let the thumb go down across all the chord's strings. Listen to Em and Am.
l241.c2b: Em, Am, Em, Am: four strokes on each.
l241.pulse: Tap the screen on each beat. Halfway, the click stops: keep going.
l241.strum: Strum Em and Am with your thumb in quarter notes, in time.
l241.strum2: Strum G and C with your thumb in quarter notes, in time.

l242.title: Eighth notes with the index
l242.objective: Strum eighth notes with your index, down on the beat and up on the "and", at 60 bpm.
l242.s1: "To strum faster, use your index: down and up."
l242.s2: Down with the back of the finger, up with the fingertip.
l242.s3: Down on 1, up on "and". Eight strokes per bar.
l242.s4: "The hand never stops: it swings like a pendulum."
l242.c1b: The index goes down with the back of the finger on the beat and up with the fingertip on the "and". Listen to C and G.
l242.c2b: Even when you don't play, the hand keeps moving. That way you don't lose the pulse.
l242.tap: Tap ↓ on each beat and ↑ on each "and".
l242.strum: Strum C and G in eighth notes with your index, in time.

l243.title: Pop strum
l243.objective: Play the pop strum (down, down-up, up-down-up) over G, C, D and Em.
l243.s1: "The strum you hear in thousands of songs."
l243.s3: On beat 3 the hand goes down without touching: that gap gives it groove.
l243.c1b: Down on 1; down and up on 2; on 3 you don't play, you only go up on its "and"; down and up on 4. Listen.
l243.c2b: G, C, D and Em, one bar each.
l243.q1: In the pop strum, what happens on beat 3?
l243.q1o2: The hand goes down without touching the strings
l243.strum: Play the pop strum over G, C, D and Em, in time.

l244.title: Ballad strum
l244.objective: Play a slow ballad strum over Am, Dm, E7 and Am at 60 bpm.
l244.s1: "For slow songs, a strum with space."
l244.s2: Down on 1, up on the "and" of 2, down on 3 and down-up on 4.
l244.s3: Let each stroke ring: don't rush.
l244.s4: "Am, Dm, E7, Am: it sounds like a sad song."
l244.c1b: Few strokes, each one ringing. Listen to Am and Dm.
l244.c2b: Am, Dm, E7 and Am: E7 leads back to Am.
l244.tap: Tap ↓ and ↑ alternately, one per eighth note.
l244.strum: Play the ballad strum over Am, Dm, E7 and Am, in time.

l245.title: The slap
l245.objective: Mark beats 2 and 4 with a slap (a strum muted with the palm) over Am and E7.
l245.s1: "Hear that dry hit in folk and rock? That's the slap."
l245.s2: Strum and, in the same motion, drop your palm on the strings: it goes "chk".
l245.s3: On 1 and 3 the chord rings; on 2 and 4, a slap.
l245.s4: "It's like having a drummer in your picking hand."
l245.c1b: The hand strums down and the palm lands right away on the strings, near the soundhole, muting them.
l245.c2b: Am and E7: chord on 1 and 3, slap on 2 and 4. Listen.
l245.q1: What does the palm do in a slap?
l245.q1o1: Lands on the strings and mutes them
l245.strum: Strum Am and E7 with a slap on 2 and 4, in time.
l245.strum2: Strum D and A7 with a slap on 2 and 4, in time.

l251.title: p-i-m-a over chords
l251.objective: Play the p-i-m-a arpeggio over C, Am, Dm and G7 at 70 bpm.
l251.s1: "The arpeggio from level 1, now with fretted chords."
l251.s2: p on the chord's bass, then i, m and a on the 3rd, 2nd and 1st strings.
l251.s3: Fret the chord before beat 1 and keep it down the whole bar.
l251.s4: "C, Am, Dm, G7: this is real accompaniment!"
l251.c1b: The thumb plays the bass (the lowest note of the chord) and the fingers climb. Listen.
l251.c2b: On C the thumb goes to the 5th string; on Dm, the 4th; on G7, the 6th. Check the diagram before you play.
l251.pads: Tap p, i, m, a in order, one tap per beat.
l251.play: Play p-i-m-a over C, Am, Dm and G7, in time.

l252.title: p-a-m-i: going down
l252.objective: Play the descending p-a-m-i arpeggio over G, Em, C and D at 70 bpm.
l252.s1: "Now the other way: the thumb on the bass and the fingers come down from the 1st string."
l252.s2: p on the bass, a on the 1st, m on the 2nd and i on the 3rd.
l252.s3: The ring finger is the weakest: give it time.
l252.s4: "G, Em, C, D: it sounds like a ballad."
l252.c1b: After the bass, the fingers come down like a waterfall. Listen.
l252.c2b: If the 1st string sounds weak, place your ring finger a little deeper on the string.
l252.pads: Tap p, a, m, i in order, one tap per beat.
l252.play: Play p-a-m-i over G, Em, C and D, in time.

l253.title: Alternating bass
l253.objective: Alternate two basses with your thumb while m plays the 2nd string, over C and G at 70 bpm.
l253.s1: "The thumb doesn't always have to play the same bass."
l253.s2: Beat 1: the chord's bass. Beat 3: the bass on the next string.
l253.s3: Between basses, m plays the 2nd string.
l253.s4: "That's how folk and milonga accompaniment sounds."
l253.c1b: On C: C on the 5th string and E on the 4th. On G: G on the 6th and B on the 5th. Listen.
l253.c2b: The thumb goes back and forth between two neighboring strings; the fingers barely move.
l253.pads: Alternate p and m, one tap per beat.
l253.play: Play the alternating bass over C and G, in time.

l254.title: Ballad arpeggio
l254.objective: Play the p-i-m-a-m-i-m-i arpeggio in eighth notes over Am, Dm, E7 and Am at 60 bpm.
l254.s1: "The ballad arpeggio: up and back, in eighth notes."
l254.s2: p, i, m, a, m, i, m, i: eight notes per bar.
l254.s3: Count "1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and": one note on each.
l254.s4: "Slow and even: no note should stick out."
l254.c1b: The thumb on 1 and the fingers draw a wave. Listen at 60 bpm.
l254.c2b: If one note is louder, play softer with that finger until it matches.
l254.pads: Tap p, i, m, a in order, one tap per beat.
l254.play: Play the ballad arpeggio over Am, Dm, E7 and Am, in time.

l255.title: Steady bass
l255.objective: Keep your thumb alternating basses in eighth notes while m and a answer, over C, Am, Dm and G7 at 60 bpm.
l255.s1: "Fingerpicking: the thumb is a clock and the fingers talk on top."
l255.s2: Thumb on every beat, alternating two basses.
l255.s3: Between beats, m or a play the 2nd or 1st string.
l255.s4: "First the thumb alone; when it's steady, add the fingers."
l255.c1b: The thumb never stops: bass, bass, bass, bass. The fingers go on the "and". Listen.
l255.c2b: If you get stuck, play only the basses for a bar, then add the fingers.
l255.pads: Alternate p and m, one tap per beat.
l255.play: Play the steady bass over C, Am, Dm and G7, in time.

l261.title: Whole step and half step
l261.objective: Recognize a half step (1 fret) and a whole step (2 frets) on the fretboard and by ear.
l261.s1: "Music is measured in steps: half steps and whole steps."
l261.s2: One fret up is a half step.
l261.s3: Two frets are a whole step.
l261.s4: "Every scale is built from these two steps."
l261.c1b: From the open 1st string (E) to fret 1 (F): a half step, the smallest distance. Listen.
l261.c2b: From E to fret 2 (F♯): a whole step, two half steps. Listen.
l261.q1: How many frets are in a whole step?
l261.ear: Listen to two notes. Are they a half step or a whole step apart?
l261.ear2: Listen to two more notes. Half step or whole step?
l261.tap: On the 1st string: go up a half step from open, then a whole step more.
l261.play: On the 1st string: open, a half step up, open again and a whole step up.

l262.title: The major scale
l262.objective: Build the major scale (W W H W W W H) and play C major in first position.
l262.s1: "Do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, ti, do: the scale everyone knows."
l262.s2: Its recipe: whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.
l262.s3: On the classical guitar, C major starts on fret 3 of the 5th string.
l262.s4: "E-F and B-C are a half step apart: those are the two short steps."
l262.c1b: C (5th string, fret 3), D and E on the 4th, F on the 4th, G and A on the 3rd, B and C on the 2nd. Listen.
l262.c2b: W W H W W W H. Starting on any note, that recipe gives its major scale.
l262.q1: What is the recipe for the major scale?
l262.q1o1: W W H W W W H
l262.q1o2: W H W W H W W
l262.q1o3: H W W W H W W
l262.tap: Press the C major scale on the fretboard, from C to C.
l262.play: Play the C major scale going up, in time.

l263.title: Major and minor triads
l263.objective: Know which notes a chord is made of and tell major from minor by ear.
l263.s1: "A chord is a triad: three stacked notes."
l263.s2: Root, third and fifth. If the third is major, the chord is major.
l263.s3: If the third is minor, a half step lower, the chord is minor.
l263.s4: "Major sounds happy; minor, sad. Your ear already knows."
l263.c1b: C: C, E, G. Am: A, C, E. Listen to the difference in color.
l263.c2b: E and Em, A and Am: between major and minor only one note changes, the third.
l263.q1: Which notes are in a major triad?
l263.ear1: Listen to the chord. Is it major or minor?
l263.ear2: Listen to the chord. Is it major or minor?
l263.ear3: Listen to the chord. Is it major or minor?
l263.play: Play the C triad (C, E, G) and then the Am triad (A, C, E), note by note.

l264.title: Chords I, IV and V
l264.objective: Find the I, IV and V chords of a key and play I-IV-V-I in G.
l264.s1: "Three chords are enough for thousands of songs."
l264.s2: In every major scale, the chords on the 1st, 4th and 5th notes are major.
l264.s3: In G major: G (I), C (IV) and D (V).
l264.s4: "V always wants to go back to I."
l264.c1b: G, C, D and G. Listen to how D "wants" to go back to G.
l264.c2b: In C major, I is C, IV is F and V is G. The barre F comes in level 3.
l264.q1: In C major, which chord is IV?
l264.q2: In G major, which chord is V?
l264.strum: Strum G, C, D and G (I-IV-V-I) in quarter notes, in time.

l265.title: The capo
l265.objective: Use a capo to change key without changing the chord shapes.
l265.s1: "Is the song too low to sing? The capo fixes it."
l265.s2: The capo presses all the strings at one fret, like a new nut.
l265.s3: With the capo on fret 2, the G shape sounds as A.
l265.s4: "The shapes are the same: only the sound changes."
l265.c1b: For every fret you move the capo up, everything sounds a half step higher.
l265.c2b: Just behind the fret, straight and not too tight. Then retune.
l265.q1: With the capo on fret 2, how does the G shape sound?
l265.strum: With the capo on fret 2 (if you have one), strum G, C, D and G, in time.

l271.title: The minor pentatonic
l271.objective: Play the A minor pentatonic in first position, from the 6th string to the 1st.
l271.s1: "Five notes that sound good over almost anything: the pentatonic."
l271.s2: A, C, D, E and G. In first position, two notes per string.
l271.s3: Many are open strings: very comfortable on the classical guitar.
l271.s4: "It's the scale of blues, rock and zamba."
l271.c1b: 6th: open and 3. 5th: open and 3. 4th: open and 2. 3rd: open and 2. 2nd: 1 and 3. 1st: open and 3. Listen.
l271.c2b: A, C, D, E, G: the major scale without its 4th and 7th notes.
l271.q1: Which notes are in the A minor pentatonic?
l271.tap: Press the pentatonic notes on the 6th, 5th and 4th strings.
l271.play: Play the pentatonic from the 6th string to the 1st, note by note.

l272.title: Pentatonic with i-m
l272.objective: Play the pentatonic up and down alternating i-m, at 70 bpm.
l272.s1: "Now in time and with alternating fingers."
l272.s2: i-m on every note, also when changing strings.
l272.s3: Go up from the 6th to the 1st and back.
l272.s4: "When it's clean, you can start improvising."
l272.c1b: Twelve notes up and twelve down, one per beat. Listen.
l272.c2b: On the three bass strings you can use your thumb; on the trebles, i-m. Try both.
l272.pads: Alternate i and m, one tap per beat.
l272.play: Play the pentatonic up and down, in time.

l273.title: Short phrases
l273.objective: Play a call phrase and an answer phrase with the pentatonic.
l273.s1: "A scale isn't music until it says something."
l273.s2: A phrase that asks: it goes up and hangs in the air.
l273.s3: One that answers: it comes down and back to A.
l273.s4: "Call and response: that's how you talk with the guitar."
l273.c1b: Two bars that go up and end on a long note. Listen.
l273.c2b: Two bars that come down and end on A, the root.
l273.call: Play the call phrase, in time.
l273.answer: Play the answer phrase, in time.

l274.title: Improvising over Am
l274.objective: Improvise with the A pentatonic over an Am and Dm backing track, playing at least 12 notes.
l274.s1: "Today you invent. There are no wrong notes if they're in the scale."
l274.s2: The band plays Am and Dm; you use the five notes.
l274.s3: Play short phrases and leave space.
l274.s4: "End your phrases on A: it sounds like a full stop."
l274.c1b: Am, Am, Dm, Am. Listen to it before you play.
l274.c2b: Repeat a phrase you like, change its ending, leave space. Less is more.
l274.improv: Improvise with the A pentatonic over the track. Play at least 12 notes.

l275.title: 12-bar blues
l275.objective: Strum the 12-bar blues in A (A7, D7, E7) and improvise one chorus with the pentatonic.
l275.s1: "The blues has a fixed form: 12 bars that repeat."
l275.s2: Four bars of A7, two of D7, two of A7, E7, D7, A7 and E7.
l275.s3: The final E7 takes you back to the start.
l275.s4: "Over that form, the A pentatonic sounds bluesy."
l275.c1b: A7 A7 A7 A7 · D7 D7 A7 A7 · E7 D7 A7 E7. Listen to the whole chorus.
l275.c2b: Count in fours: that way you always know where you are.
l275.q1: How many bars are in the blues form?
l275.strum: Strum the 12-bar blues in quarter notes, in time.
l275.improv: Improvise one chorus with the A pentatonic over the blues. Play at least 16 notes.

cp2.intro: Show what you learned in level 2: ear, strumming, the p-i-m-a arpeggio and the pentatonic.
cp2.ear: Listen to the chord. Is it major or minor?
cp2.strum: Play the pop strum over G, Em7, Am7 and D7, twice, in time.
cp2.arp: Play p-i-m-a over G, Em7, Am7 and D7, in time.
cp2.penta: Play the call and the answer with the pentatonic, in time.

l311.title: F major seventh (Fmaj7)
l311.objective: Fret F major seventh (Fmaj7), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l311.s1: "A new chord for the album: F major seventh (Fmaj7)."
l311.s2: Finger 3 on fret 3 of the 4th string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd and finger 1 on fret 1 of the 2nd; the open 1st rings. Don't play the 6th or 5th.
l311.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l311.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l311.c1t: How to fret F major seventh (Fmaj7)
l311.c1b: Finger 3 on fret 3 of the 4th string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd and finger 1 on fret 1 of the 2nd; the open 1st rings. Don't play the 6th or 5th. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l311.c2b: It's the step before F: the same shape, still without a barre. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l311.tap: Press the notes of F major seventh (Fmaj7) on the fretboard.
l311.arp: Fret F major seventh (Fmaj7) and play string by string, from low to high.
l311.strum: Strum F major seventh (Fmaj7) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l313.title: F major with a half barre (F)
l313.objective: Fret F major with a half barre (F), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l313.s1: "A new chord for the album: F major with a half barre (F)."
l313.s2: Finger 1 lying across fret 1 on the 2nd and 1st strings, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd and finger 3 on fret 3 of the 4th. Play the 4th to the 1st.
l313.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l313.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l313.c1t: How to fret F major with a half barre (F)
l313.c1b: Finger 1 lying across fret 1 on the 2nd and 1st strings, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd and finger 3 on fret 3 of the 4th. Play the 4th to the 1st. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l313.c2b: It's Fmaj7 with finger 1 laid flat: now the 1st string sounds F too. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l313.tap: Press the notes of F major with a half barre (F) on the fretboard.
l313.arp: Fret F major with a half barre (F) and play string by string, from low to high.
l313.strum: Strum F major with a half barre (F) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l314.title: B minor on 4 strings (Bm)
l314.objective: Fret B minor on 4 strings (Bm), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l314.s1: "A new chord for the album: B minor on 4 strings (Bm)."
l314.s2: Finger 1 on fret 2 of the 1st string, finger 2 on fret 3 of the 2nd, finger 3 on fret 4 of the 4th and finger 4 on fret 4 of the 3rd. Play the 4th to the 1st.
l314.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l314.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l314.c1t: How to fret B minor on 4 strings (Bm)
l314.c1b: Finger 1 on fret 2 of the 1st string, finger 2 on fret 3 of the 2nd, finger 3 on fret 4 of the 4th and finger 4 on fret 4 of the 3rd. Play the 4th to the 1st. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l314.c2b: Four fingers, four strings: the easy Bm. The full barre version comes in 3.3. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l314.tap: Press the notes of B minor on 4 strings (Bm) on the fretboard.
l314.arp: Fret B minor on 4 strings (Bm) and play string by string, from low to high.
l314.strum: Strum B minor on 4 strings (Bm) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l321.title: F major barre chord (F)
l321.objective: Fret F major barre chord (F), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l321.s1: "A new chord for the album: F major barre chord (F)."
l321.s2: Barre with finger 1 across fret 1 on all 6 strings, finger 3 on fret 3 of the 5th, finger 4 on fret 3 of the 4th and finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd.
l321.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l321.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l321.c1t: How to fret F major barre chord (F)
l321.c1b: Barre with finger 1 across fret 1 on all 6 strings, finger 3 on fret 3 of the 5th, finger 4 on fret 3 of the 4th and finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l321.c2b: It's the E shape moved up one fret, with finger 1 acting as the nut. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l321.tap: Press the notes of F major barre chord (F) on the fretboard.
l321.arp: Fret F major barre chord (F) and play string by string, from low to high.
l321.strum: Strum F major barre chord (F) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l322.title: F minor (Fm)
l322.objective: Fret F minor (Fm), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l322.s1: "A new chord for the album: F minor (Fm)."
l322.s2: Like the barre F without finger 2: the 3rd string sounds under the barre on fret 1.
l322.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l322.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l322.c1b: Like the barre F without finger 2: the 3rd string sounds under the barre on fret 1. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l322.c2b: The Em shape, moved up. If the 3rd string doesn't ring, roll finger 1 slightly onto its side. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l322.tap: Press the notes of F minor (Fm) on the fretboard.
l322.arp: Fret F minor (Fm) and play string by string, from low to high.
l322.strum: Strum F minor (Fm) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l323.title: F seventh (F7)
l323.objective: Fret F seventh (F7), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l323.s1: "A new chord for the album: F seventh (F7)."
l323.s2: Barre on fret 1, finger 3 on fret 3 of the 5th string and finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd.
l323.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l323.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l323.c1b: Barre on fret 1, finger 3 on fret 3 of the 5th string and finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l323.c2b: The E7 shape, moved up: it works for blues in any key. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l323.tap: Press the notes of F seventh (F7) on the fretboard.
l323.arp: Fret F seventh (F7) and play string by string, from low to high.
l323.strum: Strum F seventh (F7) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l331.title: B flat major (B♭)
l331.objective: Fret B flat major (B♭), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l331.s1: "A new chord for the album: B flat major (B♭)."
l331.s2: Barre on fret 1 from the 5th string to the 1st, and fingers 2, 3 and 4 on fret 3 of the 4th, 3rd and 2nd. Don't play the 6th.
l331.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l331.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l331.c1t: How to fret B flat major (B♭)
l331.c1b: Barre on fret 1 from the 5th string to the 1st, and fingers 2, 3 and 4 on fret 3 of the 4th, 3rd and 2nd. Don't play the 6th. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l331.c2b: It's the A shape moved up one fret. The root is on the 5th string: that's where the thumb starts. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l331.tap: Press the notes of B flat major (B♭) on the fretboard.
l331.arp: Fret B flat major (B♭) and play string by string, from low to high.
l331.strum: Strum B flat major (B♭) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l332.title: B flat minor (B♭m)
l332.objective: Fret B flat minor (B♭m), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l332.s1: "A new chord for the album: B flat minor (B♭m)."
l332.s2: Barre on fret 1 from the 5th string, finger 3 on fret 3 of the 4th, finger 4 on fret 3 of the 3rd and finger 2 on fret 2 of the 2nd.
l332.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l332.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l332.c1t: How to fret B flat minor (B♭m)
l332.c1b: Barre on fret 1 from the 5th string, finger 3 on fret 3 of the 4th, finger 4 on fret 3 of the 3rd and finger 2 on fret 2 of the 2nd. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l332.c2b: The Am shape, moved up. On fret 2 it's the full barre Bm. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l332.tap: Press the notes of B flat minor (B♭m) on the fretboard.
l332.arp: Fret B flat minor (B♭m) and play string by string, from low to high.
l332.strum: Strum B flat minor (B♭m) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l333.title: B minor seventh (Bm7)
l333.objective: Fret B minor seventh (Bm7), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l333.s1: "A new chord for the album: B minor seventh (Bm7)."
l333.s2: Barre on fret 2 from the 5th string, finger 3 on fret 4 of the 4th and finger 2 on fret 3 of the 2nd.
l333.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l333.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l333.c1t: How to fret B minor seventh (Bm7)
l333.c1b: Barre on fret 2 from the 5th string, finger 3 on fret 4 of the 4th and finger 2 on fret 3 of the 2nd. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l333.c2b: The Am7 shape, moved up. It sounds soft: common in bossa and jazz. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l333.tap: Press the notes of B minor seventh (Bm7) on the fretboard.
l333.arp: Fret B minor seventh (Bm7) and play string by string, from low to high.
l333.strum: Strum B minor seventh (Bm7) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l342.title: B seventh (B7)
l342.objective: Fret B seventh (B7), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l342.s1: "A new chord for the album: B seventh (B7)."
l342.s2: Finger 2 on fret 2 of the 5th string, finger 1 on fret 1 of the 4th, finger 3 on fret 2 of the 3rd and finger 4 on fret 2 of the 1st; the open 2nd rings. Don't play the 6th.
l342.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l342.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l342.c1b: Finger 2 on fret 2 of the 5th string, finger 1 on fret 1 of the 4th, finger 3 on fret 2 of the 3rd and finger 4 on fret 2 of the 1st; the open 2nd rings. Don't play the 6th. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l342.c2b: It's the V chord of the blues in E: it leads back to E7. Listen to it in the p-i-m-i pattern.
l342.tap: Press the notes of B seventh (B7) on the fretboard.
l342.arp: Fret B seventh (B7) and play string by string, from low to high.
l342.strum: Strum B seventh (B7) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l312.title: Finger 1 pressure
l312.objective: Lay finger 1 across the 2nd and 1st strings at fret 1 and make both ring clean.
l312.s1: "Before the full barre, a tiny barre: two strings."
l312.s2: Lay finger 1 across the 2nd and 1st strings, just behind fret 1.
l312.s3: Use the side of the finger that faces the headstock: it's harder.
l312.s4: "Don't squeeze with your thumb: pull your arm back a little."
l312.c1b: Look at the diagram: finger 1 covers two strings. Roll it slightly toward the nut so the bone does the work.
l312.c2b: The 2nd string sounds C and the 1st sounds F. Play them alternately: both have to ring clean.
l312.q1: Which part of finger 1 should you use for a barre?
l312.q1o2: The side that faces the headstock
l312.play: With finger 1 laid across fret 1, play the 2nd and 1st strings alternately, in time.

l324.title: Moving the barre
l324.objective: Move the Em barre shape: Fm on fret 1, F#m on fret 2 and Gm on fret 3.
l324.s1: "The best thing about barres: one shape, many chords."
l324.s2: Fm, F#m and Gm are the same shape on frets 1, 2 and 3.
l324.s3: The note on the 6th string tells you the chord's name.
l324.s4: "Move up one fret and the chord goes up a half step."
l324.c1b: The same shape, one fret higher each time. Listen, in half notes.
l324.c2b: The thumb plays the 6th string: F, F# and G.
l324.tap: Press the notes of F#m on the fretboard.
l324.tap2: Press the notes of Gm on the fretboard.
l324.strum: Strum Fm, F#m, Gm and F#m in half notes, in time.
l324.pimi: Play Fm, F#m, Gm and F#m in p-i-m-i, in time.

l325.title: Open to barre
l325.objective: Change between open and barre chords without breaking the pulse: C, F, G and C; Am, F#m, D and E.
l325.s1: "Now let's mix: open chords and barres in the same song."
l325.s2: From C to F: finger 3 drops to the 4th string and finger 1 lies flat.
l325.s3: Get the barre ready on beat 4 of the previous bar.
l325.s4: "If the barre is late, play beat 1 anyway: what matters is not stopping."
l325.c1b: The half-barre F between two open chords. Listen.
l325.c2b: The thumb goes to the 5th string on C, the 4th on F and the 6th on G.
l325.strum1: Strum Am, F#m, D and E in quarter notes, in time.
l325.strum: Strum C, F, G and C in quarter notes, in time.
l325.pimi: Play C, F, G and C in p-i-m-i, in time.

l334.title: Moving the A shape
l334.objective: Move the Am barre shape: Cm on fret 3 and C#m on fret 4.
l334.s1: "The A shape moves too. Its root is on the 5th string."
l334.s2: Cm: barre on fret 3. C#m: the same shape on fret 4.
l334.s3: The note on the 5th string gives the name: C on fret 3, C# on fret 4.
l334.s4: "With two shapes, E and A, you have every major and minor chord."
l334.c1b: The Am shape on frets 3 and 4. Listen, in half notes.
l334.c2b: The thumb plays the 5th string: C and C#.
l334.tap: Press the notes of C#m on the fretboard.
l334.q1: Which fret does the C#m barre go on?
l334.strum: Strum Cm and C#m in half notes, in time.
l334.pimi: Play Cm and C#m in p-i-m-i, in time.

l335.title: Barres only
l335.objective: Play a progression made only of barre chords: B♭, Gm, Cm and F7.
l335.s1: "No open strings: everything with a barre."
l335.s2: B♭ (A shape, fret 1), Gm (E shape, fret 3).
l335.s3: Cm (A shape, fret 3) and F7 (E7 shape, fret 1).
l335.s4: "If your hand gets tired, relax it between chords."
l335.c1b: One bar each, in quarter notes. Listen.
l335.c2b: The thumb jumps between the 5th and 6th strings: check each chord's diagram.
l335.strum: Strum B♭, Gm, Cm and F7 in quarter notes, in time.
l335.pimi: Play B♭, Gm, Cm and F7 in p-i-m-i, in time.

l341.title: The dominant seventh
l341.objective: Recognize a seventh chord by ear and play C7 resolving to F.
l341.s1: "A major chord with one more note: the seventh. It sounds like something is about to happen."
l341.s2: C is C, E, G. C7 adds B flat.
l341.s3: That tension wants to resolve: C7 goes to F.
l341.s4: "That's why the blues is full of sevenths."
l341.c1b: Look at the C7 diagram: it's C with finger 4 on fret 3 of the 3rd string. Listen to the difference.
l341.c2b: C7 and then F: the tension lets go.
l341.ear1: Listen to the chord. Is it a triad or does it have a seventh?
l341.ear2: Listen to the chord. Is it a triad or does it have a seventh?
l341.tap: Press the notes of C7 on the fretboard.
l341.strum: Strum C7 and F in quarter notes, in time.

l343.title: The boogie bass
l343.objective: Play a boogie bass (root, third, fifth and sixth) with your thumb over E7 and A7 at 70 bpm.
l343.s1: "The blues walks: the bass goes up and down the chord."
l343.s2: On E: E, G#, B, C#. On A: A, C#, E, F#.
l343.s3: The thumb does all the work; i rests.
l343.s4: "In the blues, eighth notes are played uneven, "long-short": that's the shuffle. For now, in quarter notes."
l343.c1b: Four bars: E, A, E and back. Listen with the metronome.
l343.c2b: Once it's steady, try it "long-short", like the band's blues track.
l343.tap: Alternate p and i, one tap per beat.
l343.play: Play the boogie bass with your thumb, in time.

l344.title: Blues in E and A
l344.objective: Strum the 12-bar blues in E (E7, A7, B7) and in A (A7, D7, E7).
l344.s2: In E: E7 is I, A7 is IV and B7 is V.
l344.s3: In A: A7, D7 and E7.
l344.s4: "If you know the degrees, you know the blues in any key."
l344.c1b: E7 E7 E7 E7 · A7 A7 E7 E7 · B7 A7 E7 B7. Listen.
l344.c2b: A7 A7 A7 A7 · D7 D7 A7 A7 · E7 D7 A7 E7. Listen.
l344.q1: In the blues in E, which chord is V?
l344.strum1: Strum the blues in E in quarter notes, in time.
l344.strum2: Strum the blues in A in quarter notes, in time.

l345.title: The turnaround
l345.objective: Play a turnaround in E that walks down by half steps and ends on B7, to go back to the start of the blues.
l345.s1: "At the end of every blues chorus there's a little lick: the turnaround."
l345.s2: E, D, C#, C: it walks down by half steps.
l345.s3: It ends on B, the bass of B7, which takes you back to E7.
l345.s4: "It's the blues signature: it sounds like "one more time"."
l345.c1b: Four quarter notes going down by half steps and two half notes on B. Listen.
l345.c2b: After the turnaround, fret B7: it's the chord that starts it all again.
l345.q1o1: Going back to the start of the form
l345.play: Play the turnaround in E, in time.
l345.b7: Fret B7 and play its fretted notes, from low to high.

l351.title: Ascending slur
l351.objective: Make a higher note sound without plucking, by hammering with a fretting finger.
l351.s1: "Can you play a note without plucking it? Yes: by hammering."
l351.s2: Pluck the open 3rd string and drop finger 2 onto fret 2, firm and fast.
l351.s3: You hear G and then A, from one pluck of the picking hand.
l351.s4: "Hit with the tip, like a tiny hammer."
l351.c1b: Look at the drawing: the finger falls from above, just behind the fret. The string keeps vibrating and the note goes up.
l351.c2b: G to A on the 3rd string, and C to D on the 2nd. Listen.
l351.q1: In an ascending slur, how does the second note sound?
l351.q1o1: The fretting finger drops onto the string
l351.play: Ascending slur on the 3rd string: open and fret 2, several times.
l351.play2: Ascending slur on the 2nd string: frets 1 and 3, several times.

l352.title: Descending slur
l352.objective: Make a lower note sound without plucking, by pulling the string with the finger that lifts off.
l352.s1: "Now the other way: from a high note to a low one, without plucking."
l352.s2: With fingers 1 and 3 on the 2nd string, pluck and take finger 3 off, pulling the string down.
l352.s3: You hear D and then C.
l352.s4: "Don't just lift: drag the finger a little, as if plucking with your fretting hand."
l352.c1b: Look at the drawing: the finger that leaves catches the string and releases it. The lower finger must already be in place.
l352.c2b: D to C on the 2nd string, and G to E on the 1st. Listen.
l352.q1: For a descending slur, what must be in place first?
l352.q1o2: The finger for the lower note
l352.play: Descending slur on the 2nd string: fret 3 to fret 1, several times.
l352.play2: Descending slur on the 1st string: fret 3 to open, several times.

l353.title: The slide
l353.objective: Move from one note to another by sliding the finger along the string, without plucking again.
l353.s1: "A slide is a slur that travels: the finger glides from fret to fret."
l353.s2: Press fret 3 on the 1st string, pluck and slide to fret 5 without letting go.
l353.s3: You hear G arriving at A, passing through in between.
l353.s4: "If you let up, the note dies on the way."
l353.c1b: Look at the drawing: keep the pressure while the finger travels. You pluck only once.
l353.c2b: From 3 to 5 and from 5 to 3, on the 1st string. Listen.
l353.play: Slide on the 1st string: from fret 3 to 5 and back.
l353.play2: Slide on the 2nd string: from fret 3 to 5 and back.

l354.title: The trill
l354.objective: Alternate fast ascending and descending slurs between the open 1st string and fret 1.
l354.s1: "Slur up, slur down, very fast: a trill."
l354.s2: E, F, E, F… from a single pluck of the picking hand.
l354.s3: Finger 1 hammers and pulls, over and over.
l354.s4: "Start slow. Speed comes on its own."
l354.c1b: Even eighth notes between the open 1st string and fret 1. Listen.
l354.c2b: If the finger gets tired, stop and shake out your hand. A tense trill sounds uneven.
l354.play: Trill on the 1st string: open and fret 1, alternating, without plucking again.

l355.title: Pentatonic ornaments
l355.objective: Play an A pentatonic phrase with ascending and descending slurs.
l355.s2: Two notes per string: pluck the first, slur the second.
l355.s3: Going up, an ascending slur; going down, a descending one.
l355.s4: "That's how blues and folk solos sound."
l355.c1b: Four bars in first position: up with ascending slurs and down with descending ones. Listen.
l355.c2b: Pluck only the first note on each string. The rest come from the fretting hand.
l355.tab: Read the phrase and tap each note on the fretboard.
l355.play: Play the phrase with slurs, note by note.

l361.title: The blue note
l361.objective: Add the blue note (E♭) to the A pentatonic and use it in passing between D and E.
l361.s1: "One single note turns the pentatonic into blues."
l361.s2: Between D and E is E♭: the blue note.
l361.s3: On the 4th string: open, fret 1, fret 2. D, E♭, E.
l361.s4: "Use it in passing: don't sit on it too long."
l361.c1b: The blue note passes quickly and lands on E. Listen.
l361.c2b: E♭ rubs a little against the chord, and that rub is the color of the blues.
l361.q1: Which note does the blues scale add to the A pentatonic?
l361.play: Play D, E♭, E, G, A and C, in time.

l362.title: The blues scale
l362.objective: Play the A blues scale in first position, from the 6th string to the 1st.
l362.s1: "Pentatonic plus blue note: the full blues scale."
l362.s2: The blue note shows up twice: on the 4th string (fret 1) and the 2nd (fret 4).
l362.s4: "With this scale you can improvise over any blues in A."
l362.c1b: From the 6th string to the 1st, with both blue notes. Listen.
l362.c2b: The blue note on the 2nd string is on fret 4: use your little finger.
l362.tap: Press D, E♭ and E on the 4th string.
l362.play: Play the blues scale from the 6th string to the 1st, note by note.

l363.title: The major pentatonic
l363.objective: Play the C major pentatonic and know it has the same notes as the A minor one.
l363.s1: "A trick: the A minor pentatonic and the C major one are the same."
l363.s2: C, D, E, G, A: it starts and ends on C.
l363.s3: Over major chords it sounds happy, like pop and country.
l363.s4: "Same notes, different home: the root decides."
l363.c1b: From the C on the 5th string to the A on the 1st. Listen.
l363.c2b: End on A and it sounds minor; end on C and it sounds major.
l363.q1: What do the A minor pentatonic and the C major pentatonic have in common?
l363.play: Play the C major pentatonic, note by note.

l364.title: Boxes 1 and 2
l364.objective: Play the A pentatonic in box 1 (fret 5) and box 2 (fret 7).
l364.s1: "The pentatonic also lives higher up the neck."
l364.s2: Box 1: from fret 5, with the root A on the 6th string.
l364.s3: Box 2: the next one, from fret 7.
l364.s4: "On a classical guitar you reach up to fret 12 comfortably."
l364.c1b: Two notes per string, frets 5 to 8. Listen.
l364.c2b: It starts where box 1 ends: frets 7 to 10. Listen.
l364.tap: Press the box 2 notes on the 6th, 5th and 4th strings.

l365.title: Major and minor
l365.objective: Improvise with the blues scale over a blues in A and with the major pentatonic over C, Am, F and G.
l365.s1: "Two flavors: bluesy and happy. Today you use both."
l365.s2: Over the blues in A: the blues scale.
l365.s3: Over C, Am, F and G: the C major pentatonic.
l365.s4: "Listen to the track first and choose the scale by its color."
l365.c1b: A7, D7, E7: the blues scale goes here. Listen.
l365.c2b: Bright major chords: the C major pentatonic goes here.
l365.blues: Improvise with the A blues scale over the blues. Play at least 16 notes.
l365.major: Improvise with the C major pentatonic over the track. Play at least 12 notes.

l371.title: 6/8 time
l371.objective: Feel 6/8 as two groups of three eighth notes and strum one beat per group.
l371.s1: "Until now you counted in fours. Today you count in threes."
l371.s2: A bar of 6/8 has six eighth notes: ONE two three, FOUR five six.
l371.s3: You strum on the 1st and the 4th: two strokes per bar, like a swing.
l371.s4: "It is the rhythm of the zamba and the chacarera."
l371.c1b: Am and E7 in 6/8: one stroke at the start of each group. Listen to the click.
l371.c2b: The same chords in 4/4 quarter notes. Can you hear it rocks differently?
l371.q1: How many eighth notes are in a bar of 6/8?
l371.ear: Listen: is it in 4/4 or in 6/8?
l371.strum: Strum Am and E7 in 6/8: one stroke at the start of each group of three.

l372.title: The zamba
l372.objective: Strum the zamba pattern in 6/8 and play its accompaniment with your thumb.
l372.s1: "The zamba is slow and elegant: it is danced with handkerchiefs."
l372.s2: Down, rest, down, up, down, rest.
l372.s3: With your thumb, the same zamba in quarter notes: bass and two chord notes.
l372.s4: "Your quarter notes go in threes and the band in twos: that blend is the zamba."
l372.c1b: Am, Dm, E7 and Am with the zamba pattern. Listen.
l372.c2b: Bass on 1 and two chord notes on 2 and 3. Listen.
l372.q1: In the zamba pattern, which eighth notes do you not strum?
l372.strum: Strum the zamba: Am, Dm, E7 and Am.
l372.play: Play the accompaniment with your thumb: bass and two notes per bar, in time.

l373.title: The chacarera
l373.objective: Strum the chacarera in 6/8, faster and punchier than the zamba.
l373.s1: "The chacarera is for stomping: it goes faster."
l373.s2: It is like the zamba, but the last stroke also goes up.
l373.s3: The bass drum marks beat 1 and the rest of the bar rattles.
l373.s4: "Same family as the zamba, a different character."
l373.c1b: Am, E7, Dm and E7 with the chacarera pattern. Listen.
l373.c2b: The same chords with the zamba pattern. Compare.
l373.q1: How are the eighth notes grouped in the chacarera?
l373.ear: Listen: is it a zamba or a chacarera?
l373.strum: Strum the chacarera: Am, E7, Dm and E7.

l374.title: Tango and milonga
l374.objective: Strum the tango in accented quarter notes and the milonga in 3 + 3 + 2.
l374.s1: "The tango goes back to 4/4, but every stroke is firm and short."
l374.s2: Tango: four accented strokes per bar.
l374.s3: Milonga: the eight eighth notes are grouped 3 + 3 + 2.
l374.s4: "One, two, three; one, two, three; one, two."
l374.c1b: Am, Dm, E7 and Am in accented quarter notes. Listen.
l374.c2b: The same chords with strokes on the 1st, 4th and 7th eighth notes. Listen.
l374.q1: How are the eighth notes grouped in the milonga?
l374.tango: Strum the tango in accented quarter notes: Am, Dm, E7 and Am.
l374.milonga: Strum the milonga in 3 + 3 + 2: Am, Dm, E7 and Am.

l375.title: The creole waltz
l375.objective: Play the creole waltz in 3/4: bass on 1 and the chord on 2 and 3.
l375.s1: "The creole waltz turns: one, two, three."
l375.s2: Three beats per bar. The bass on 1, the chord on 2 and 3.
l375.s3: With your thumb: bass and two chord notes, one per beat.
l375.s4: "C and G7: with two chords you already have a waltz."
l375.c1b: C, G7, G7 and C in 3/4: one stroke per beat. Listen.
l375.c2b: Bass on 1 and two chord notes on 2 and 3. Listen.
l375.q1: How many beats are in a waltz bar?
l375.strum: Strum the waltz: C, G7, G7 and C, one stroke per beat.
l375.play: Play the waltz with your thumb: bass and two notes per bar, in time.

l411.title: The chords of the scale
l411.objective: Build a chord on each note of C major and know its degree: I, II, III, IV, V and VI.
l411.s1: "Every note of the scale has its own chord."
l411.s2: C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am: major on I, IV and V; minor on II, III and VI.
l411.s4: "With these six chords you can accompany half of all popular music."
l411.c1b: C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am, G and C: one bar each. Listen.
l411.c2b: The same chords with the thumb on the bass. Listen to the scale climbing.
l411.q1: Which degree is G in C major?
l411.strum: Strum C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am, G and C in quarter notes, in time.
l411.pimi: Play C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am, G and C in p-i-m-i, in time.

l412.title: C major seventh (Cmaj7)
l412.objective: Fret C major seventh (Cmaj7), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l412.s1: "A new chord for the album: C major seventh (Cmaj7)."
l412.s2: Finger 3 on fret 3 of the 5th string and finger 2 on fret 2 of the 4th; the 3rd, 2nd and 1st open. The 6th does not sound.
l412.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l412.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l412.c1t: How to fret C major seventh (Cmaj7)
l412.c1b: Finger 3 on fret 3 of the 5th string and finger 2 on fret 2 of the 4th; the 3rd, 2nd and 1st open. The 6th does not sound. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l412.c2b: It is C without finger 1: the open 2nd string adds the seventh, B. Four different notes: a seventh chord.
l412.tap: Press the notes of C major seventh (Cmaj7) on the fretboard.
l412.arp: Fret C major seventh (Cmaj7) and play string by string, from low to high.
l412.strum: Strum C major seventh (Cmaj7) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l413.title: Functions: rest, tension and return
l413.objective: Recognize tonic, subdominant and dominant in Cmaj7, Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7, and fret Dm7.
l413.s2: Cmaj7 is home (tonic). Dm7 leaves home (subdominant).
l413.s3: G7 asks to go back (dominant) and Cmaj7 brings you home again.
l413.c1b: One bar each, in quarter notes. Listen to the tension of G7.
l413.c2b: Half barre with finger 1 on fret 1 of the 2nd and 1st strings, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd; the 4th open.
l413.q1: What function does G7 have in C major?
l413.strum: Strum Cmaj7, Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7 in quarter notes, in time.
l413.pimi: Play Cmaj7, Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7 in p-i-m-i, in time.
l413.tap: Press the notes of Dm7 on the fretboard.

l414.title: The II-V-I
l414.objective: Play the II-V-I in G major (Am7, D7, Gmaj7) and fret Gmaj7.
l414.s1: "The most famous progression in jazz: two, five, one."
l414.s2: In G: Am7 is the II, D7 the V and Gmaj7 the I.
l414.s3: Gmaj7: finger 3 on fret 3 of the 6th string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 5th and finger 1 on fret 2 of the 1st.
l414.s4: "Spot a II-V-I and you have spotted half a jazz tune."
l414.c1b: Two bars of Gmaj7 at the end to rest. Listen.
l414.c2b: The same chords with the thumb on the bass. Listen.
l414.q1: In G major, which degrees are Am7, D7 and Gmaj7?
l414.strum: Strum Am7, D7, Gmaj7 and Gmaj7 in quarter notes, in time.
l414.pimi: Play Am7, D7, Gmaj7 and Gmaj7 in p-i-m-i, in time.
l414.tap: Press the notes of Gmaj7 on the fretboard.

l415.title: The minor II-V-I
l415.objective: Play the II-V-I in A minor (Bm7♭5, E7, Am7) and fret Bm7♭5.
l415.s2: The II is half-diminished: Bm7♭5. The V is E7 and the I is Am7.
l415.s3: Bm7♭5: finger 2 on fret 2 of the 5th string, finger 3 on fret 2 of the 3rd and finger 1 on fret 1 of the 1st; the 4th and 2nd open.
l415.s4: "The ♭5 is the note that gives it that tango and bolero colour."
l415.c1b: Two bars of Am7 at the end. Listen.
l415.c2b: The same chords with the thumb on the bass. Listen.
l415.q1: What kind of chord is the II in a minor key?
l415.strum: Strum Bm7♭5, E7, Am7 and Am7 in quarter notes, in time.
l415.pimi: Play Bm7♭5, E7, Am7 and Am7 in p-i-m-i, in time.
l415.tap: Press the notes of Bm7♭5 on the fretboard.

l421.title: G minor seventh (Gm7)
l421.objective: Fret G minor seventh (Gm7), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l421.s1: "A new chord for the album: G minor seventh (Gm7)."
l421.s2: Barre on fret 3 and finger 3 on fret 5 of the 5th string. The root is on the 6th string.
l421.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l421.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l421.c1t: How to fret G minor seventh (Gm7)
l421.c1b: Barre on fret 3 and finger 3 on fret 5 of the 5th string. The root is on the 6th string. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l421.c2b: It is the Em7 shape moved to fret 3. Move it and you have any m7 with its root on the 6th string.
l421.tap: Press the notes of G minor seventh (Gm7) on the fretboard.
l421.arp: Fret G minor seventh (Gm7) and play string by string, from low to high.
l421.strum: Strum G minor seventh (Gm7) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l422.title: B-flat major seventh (B♭maj7)
l422.objective: Fret B-flat major seventh (B♭maj7), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l422.s1: "A new chord for the album: B-flat major seventh (B♭maj7)."
l422.s2: Barre on fret 1 from the 5th string, finger 3 on fret 3 of the 4th, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd and finger 4 on fret 3 of the 2nd.
l422.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l422.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l422.c1t: How to fret B-flat major seventh (B♭maj7)
l422.c1b: Barre on fret 1 from the 5th string, finger 3 on fret 3 of the 4th, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd and finger 4 on fret 3 of the 2nd. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l422.c2b: The root is on the 5th string: with this shape you can build any maj7 rooted on the 5th string.
l422.tap: Press the notes of B-flat major seventh (B♭maj7) on the fretboard.
l422.arp: Fret B-flat major seventh (B♭maj7) and play string by string, from low to high.
l422.strum: Strum B-flat major seventh (B♭maj7) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l423.title: Major II-V-I in F
l423.objective: Play the II-V-I in F major (Gm7, C7, Fmaj7) with roots on the 6th and 5th strings.
l423.s2: Gm7 rooted on the 6th string, C7 rooted on the 5th.
l423.s3: And Fmaj7, which you already know from level 3.
l423.s4: "Your hand barely moves: that is comfortable jazz playing."
l423.c1b: Two bars of Fmaj7 at the end. Listen.
l423.c2b: The thumb jumps from the 6th to the 5th and the 4th string. Listen.
l423.q1: In F major, which chord is the V7?
l423.strum: Strum Gm7, C7, Fmaj7 and Fmaj7 in quarter notes, in time.
l423.pimi: Play Gm7, C7, Fmaj7 and Fmaj7 in p-i-m-i, in time.

l424.title: Minor II-V-I in D
l424.objective: Fret Em7♭5 and A7♭9 and play the II-V-I in D minor (Em7♭5, A7♭9, Dm7).
l424.s2: Em7♭5: finger 1 on fret 1 of the 5th string and finger 3 on fret 3 of the 2nd; the rest open.
l424.s3: A7♭9: fingers 1 and 2 on fret 2 of the 4th and 2nd strings, fingers 3 and 4 on fret 3 of the 3rd and 1st.
l424.s4: "The flat nine tightens the dominant: Dm7 resolves it."
l424.c1b: Two bars of Dm7 at the end. Listen.
l424.c2b: The same chords with the thumb on the bass. Listen.
l424.strum: Strum Em7♭5, A7♭9, Dm7 and Dm7 in quarter notes, in time.
l424.pimi: Play Em7♭5, A7♭9, Dm7 and Dm7 in p-i-m-i, in time.
l424.tap1: Press the notes of Em7♭5 on the fretboard.
l424.tap2: Press the notes of A7♭9 on the fretboard.

l425.title: Comping
l425.objective: Comp two II-V-Is with the Charleston rhythm: beat 1 and the "and" of 2.
l425.s1: "In jazz, the guitar does not strum all the time: it comments."
l425.s2: The Charleston: one stroke on 1 and another on the "and" of 2.
l425.s3: The rest of the bar is silence: it leaves room for the melody.
l425.c1b: Gm7, C7 and Fmaj7 with the Charleston rhythm. Listen.
l425.c2b: The same chords in four quarter notes. Compare.
l425.q1: Where do the Charleston strokes fall?
l425.strum: Comp Gm7, C7, Fmaj7, Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7 with the Charleston rhythm.

l431.title: The bossa thumb
l431.objective: Play the bossa nova bass with your thumb: root on 1 and another low chord note on 3.
l431.s1: "Bossa nova was born in Brazil, on a nylon-string guitar."
l431.s2: The thumb is steady, like a clock: on 1 and on 3.
l431.s3: First the root, then another low note of the same chord.
l431.s4: "If the thumb does not rush, the fingers can dance."
l431.c1b: Cmaj7, Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7: two half notes per bar. Listen to the click.
l431.c2b: The thumb plays the 5th string at fret 3 and then the 4th.
l431.q1: In bossa nova, where does the thumb play?
l431.play: Play the bossa bass with your thumb, in time.

l432.title: Syncopated fingers
l432.objective: Pluck the bossa chords with i-m-a between the beats: on 1, the "and" of 2 and the "and" of 3.
l432.s1: "Now the fingers: i, m and a together, like a pinch."
l432.s2: One on 1, another on the "and" of 2 and another on the "and" of 3.
l432.s3: They fall between the beats: that is syncopation.
l432.s4: "That syncopation is the sway of bossa nova."
l432.c1b: Cmaj7, Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7 with syncopated fingers, at 60. Listen to the click.
l432.q1: What do the fingers do in bossa nova?
l432.q1o1: They always play with the thumb
l432.q1o2: They play syncopations, between the beats
l432.q1o3: They strum up on every beat
l432.ear: Listen: an even strum or bossa?
l432.strum: Play Cmaj7, Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7 with syncopated fingers.

l433.title: The batida
l433.objective: Combine thumb and fingers in the bossa batida over Dm6, G13 and Cmaj7.
l433.s1: "Thumb on 1 and 3, syncopated fingers: all together it is the batida."
l433.s2: Dm6: finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd string and finger 1 on fret 1 of the 1st; the 4th and 2nd open.
l433.s3: G13: finger 1 on fret 3 of the 6th, finger 2 on fret 3 of the 4th, finger 3 on fret 4 of the 3rd and finger 4 on fret 5 of the 2nd; the 1st open and the 5th muted.
l433.s4: "Two chords with the sound of Rio."
l433.c1b: Finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd string and finger 1 on fret 1 of the 1st. Listen to the batida.
l433.c2b: Mute the 5th string by lightly touching it with finger 1. Listen to the batida.
l433.strum: Play the batida on Dm6, G13 and Cmaj7.
l433.tap1: Press the notes of Dm6 on the fretboard.
l433.tap2: Press the notes of G13 on the fretboard.

l434.title: The 6/9 and the diminished
l434.objective: Fret C6/9 and G#dim7 and use the diminished as a passing chord into Am7.
l434.s2: C6/9: finger 2 on fret 3 of the 5th string, finger 1 flat on fret 2 of the 4th and 3rd, fingers 3 and 4 on fret 3 of the 2nd and 1st.
l434.s3: G#dim7: finger 1 flat on fret 3 from the 4th to the 2nd string, finger 2 on fret 4 of the 6th, fingers 3 and 4 on fret 4 of the 3rd and 1st.
l434.s4: "The diminished is a half step below Am7 and leads into it."
l434.c1b: Sixth and ninth: a floating C major. Listen.
l434.c2b: The bass rises from G# to A. Listen.
l434.q1: Which chord does G#dim7 lead to in this progression?
