l434.strum: Strum C6/9, G#dim7, Am7 and D7 in quarter notes, in time.
l434.tap1: Press the notes of C6/9 on the fretboard.
l434.tap2: Press the notes of G#dim7 on the fretboard.

l435.title: A bossa turn
l435.objective: Play eight bars of bossa with every chord in the module and syncopated fingers.
l435.s1: "You have everything now: let's build a full turn."
l435.s2: C6/9, G#dim7, Am7, D7: it moves through the diminished.
l435.s3: Dm6, G13 and C6/9: the II-V-I with bossa colours.
l435.s4: "Play softly: bossa is sung almost in a whisper."
l435.c1b: Eight bars with syncopated fingers. Listen.
l435.c2b: The same turn with the thumb on the bass, to learn the changes. Listen.
l435.strum: Play the bossa turn with syncopated fingers: C6/9, G#dim7, Am7, D7, Dm6, G13, C6/9 and C6/9.
l435.pimi: Play the turn in p-i-m-i, in time.

l441.title: Box 3
l441.objective: Play box 3 of the A minor pentatonic, between frets 9 and 13.
l441.s1: "The pentatonic does not stay in one place: it repeats all over the neck."
l441.s2: Box 3 starts where box 2 ends, at fret 10 of the 6th string.
l441.s3: They are the same five notes: A, C, D, E and G.
l441.s4: "One more box and the neck starts to be yours."
l441.c1b: From fret 9 to 13, from the 6th string to the 1st. Listen.
l441.c2b: Am7, Dm7, Am7 and E7: the A minor pentatonic works here.
l441.play: Play box 3 from low to high, note by note.

l442.title: Box 4
l442.objective: Play box 4 of the A minor pentatonic, from fret 12.
l442.s1: "We pass fret 12: the nylon guitar gets high."
l442.s3: At fret 12 everything repeats an octave up: the 6th string gives E again.
l442.s4: "Play softly: up here the strings are close to the body."
l442.c2b: The same progression in A minor. Listen.
l442.q1: What is the root of every box of this scale?
l442.play: Play box 4 from low to high, note by note.

l443.title: Box 5
l443.objective: Play box 5 of the A minor pentatonic, between frets 2 and 5, and connect it to box 1.
l443.s1: "The last box is down low, near the nut."
l443.s3: Its upper edge, fret 5, is the lower edge of box 1.
l443.c2b: The same progression in A minor. Listen.
l443.q1: Moving up from box 5, which box do you meet?
l443.tap: Press the first notes of box 5 on the fretboard.
l443.play: Play box 5 from low to high, note by note.

l444.title: Connecting the boxes
l444.objective: Play a phrase that climbs the 1st string and comes down the 2nd and 3rd through boxes 1, 2 and 3.
l444.s1: "Now you do not switch boxes: you travel between them."
l444.s2: On the 1st string you climb: fret 5, 8, 10 and 12.
l444.s3: You come down the 2nd and climb the 3rd again.
l444.s4: "Slide your hand with a loose thumb behind the neck."
l444.c1b: Four bars that cross three boxes. Listen to the click.
l444.c2b: It is the bridge between box 1 and box 3.
l444.q1o1: To move across the neck without breaking the phrase
l444.play: Play the phrase that connects the boxes, in time.

l445.title: The whole neck
l445.objective: Improvise with the A minor pentatonic using more than one box.
l445.s2: Start in box 1, climb to box 3 and come down to box 5.
l445.s3: The notes do not change: the place and the colour do.
l445.s4: "A phrase up high and one down low sound like two guitars."
l445.c1b: Am7, Dm7, Am7 and E7. Listen before you play.
l445.c2b: Down low, near the nut: a good place to finish.
l445.q1: If you change box, do the notes change?
l445.q1o1: No: they are the same five notes in another place
l445.q1o2: Yes, each box is a different scale
l445.improv: Improvise with the A minor pentatonic in two or more boxes. Play at least 20 notes.

l451.title: The major scale in two positions
l451.objective: Play C major in first position and G major in second position.
l451.s1: "Seven notes: the major scale is the mother of almost everything."
l451.s2: Whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.
l451.s3: In first position, C major uses the open strings; in 2nd position, G major uses none.
l451.s4: "A shape with no open strings can be moved to any key."
l451.c1b: From C to C, on the 5th, 4th, 3rd and 2nd strings. Listen.
l451.q1: What is the formula of the major scale?
l451.q1o1: W W H W W W H
l451.q1o2: W H W W H W W
l451.q1o3: W W W H W W H
l451.open: Play C major in first position, note by note.
l451.play: Play G major in 2nd position, note by note.

l452.title: Natural minor
l452.objective: Play the A natural minor scale in 5th position.
l452.s1: "The natural minor scale sounds sad and serious."
l452.s2: Whole, half, whole, whole, half, whole, whole.
l452.s3: It is the A minor pentatonic plus two notes: B and F.
l452.s4: "If you know box 1, this scale is one step away."
l452.c1b: In 5th position, from fret 5 of the 6th string. Listen.
l452.c2b: The pentatonic you already know. Compare.
l452.q1: What is the formula of the natural minor scale?
l452.q1o1: W W H W W W H
l452.q1o2: W H W W H W W
l452.q1o3: H W W W H W W
l452.play: Play A natural minor in 5th position, note by note.

l453.title: Relative keys
l453.objective: Understand that C major and A minor share the same notes and play A minor in first position.
l453.s2: C major starts on C; A minor starts on A.
l453.s3: The relative minor is a minor third below: three frets.
l453.s4: "What changes is the note you rest on."
l453.c1b: From C: it sounds happy. Listen.
l453.c2b: The same notes from A: it sounds sad. Listen.
l453.q1: What is the relative minor of C major?
l453.ear: Listen: does it sound like C major or A minor?
l453.play: Play A natural minor in first position, note by note.

l454.title: Sequences
l454.objective: Play G major in a four-note sequence, in time.
l454.s1: "Running the scale up and down is boring: sequences turn it into music."
l454.s2: Four notes from G, then four from A, then from B…
l454.s3: The same pattern, one step higher each time.
l454.s4: "That is how soloists practise: patterns, not scales."
l454.c1b: Four groups of four and G at the end. Listen to the click.
l454.c2b: G major in 2nd position, the one you already played.
l454.q1o1: The same pattern repeated from each note of the scale
l454.play: Play the four-note sequence in G major, in time.

l455.title: Arpeggios in the scale
l455.objective: Play the arpeggios of Gmaj7, Am7, Bm7 and Cmaj7 inside the 2nd position of G major.
l455.s1: "Its chords are hidden inside the scale."
l455.s2: Take every other note: G, B, D, F#. That is Gmaj7.
l455.s3: From A comes Am7; from B, Bm7; from C, Cmaj7.
l455.s4: "An arpeggio is a chord played one note at a time."
l455.c1b: Gmaj7, Am7, Bm7, Cmaj7 and G at the end. Listen to the click.
l455.c2b: The same four chords strummed. Listen.
l455.q1: Which notes make up the Gmaj7 arpeggio?
l455.play: Play the four arpeggios in 2nd position, in time.

l461.title: Question and answer
l461.objective: Play a phrase that asks (ends open, on D) and one that answers (ends on A), and improvise that way.
l461.s2: The question ends on a note that wants more: D.
l461.s3: The answer ends on the root, A, and rests.
l461.c1b: Two bars that stay open. Listen to the click.
l461.q1: Which note does the answer usually end on?
l461.play: Play the question and the answer, in time.
l461.improv: Improvise in question and answer with the A minor pentatonic. Play at least 12 notes.

l462.title: Chord tones
l462.objective: Start each bar on a note of the chord that is sounding, over Am7 and Dm7.
l462.s1: "At every chord change, aim for a note of the new chord."
l462.s2: Am7: A, C, E, G. Dm7: D, F, A, C.
l462.s3: On beat 1 of every bar, one of those notes.
l462.s4: "That way your solo draws the harmony."
l462.c1b: Every bar starts on a chord tone. Listen to the click.
l462.play: Play the phrase over Am7 and Dm7, in time.
l462.improv: Improvise over Am7 and Dm7: at each change, land on a chord tone. Play at least 16 notes.

l463.title: Improvising on the blues
l463.objective: Improvise a blues chorus in A with the blues scale, landing on a chord tone at each change.
l463.s2: When A7 sounds, aim for A or E.
l463.s3: When it moves to D7, aim for D or A; on E7, E or B.
l463.s4: "Use the blue note, E flat, in passing."
l463.c1b: A7, D7 and E7 in quarter notes. Listen before you play.
l463.c2b: E7, D7, A7 and E7: the last four bars.
l463.q1: In the A blues, which notes should you aim for when it moves to D7?
l463.q1o1: Notes of D7, like D or A
l463.improv: Improvise a blues chorus in A; at each change, land on a chord tone. Play at least 24 notes.

l464.title: Improvising over the II-V-I
l464.objective: Play an arpeggio line over Am7, D7 and Gmaj7 and improvise with the G major scale.
l464.s1: "The II-V-I asks for more than a pentatonic."
l464.s2: A line with the notes of each chord: Am7, then D7, then Gmaj7.
l464.s3: Then improvise with G major and aim for the chord tones.
l464.s4: "Arpeggios are the map; the scale is the road."
l464.c1b: Am7, D7, Gmaj7 and G. Listen to the click.
l464.c2b: Am7, D7 and two bars of Gmaj7. Listen.
l464.play: Play the arpeggio line over the II-V-I, in time.
l464.improv: Improvise with G major over the II-V-I; at each change, land on a chord tone. Play at least 16 notes.

l465.title: Bossa melody
l465.objective: Play an original bossa melody over Cmaj7, Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7, and improvise with C major.
l465.s1: "In bossa nova, the melody sings softly over the chords."
l465.s2: Four bars on the high strings, in first position.
l465.s3: Every bar starts on a chord tone.
l465.s4: "Then make up your own melody over the same progression."
l465.c1b: Four bars over Cmaj7, Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7. Listen to the click.
l465.c2b: The same progression with syncopated fingers. Listen.
l465.play: Play the bossa melody, in time.
l465.improv: Improvise with C major over the bossa progression; at each change, land on a chord tone. Play at least 16 notes.

cp4.intro: Show what you learned in level 4: major and minor II-V-I, comping, the bossa turn and improvising over the changes.
cp4.ear: Listen to the progression. Is it a major or a minor II-V-I?
cp4.comping: Comp the two II-V-Is with the Charleston rhythm, in time.
cp4.bossa: Play the bossa turn with syncopated fingers, in time.
cp4.improv: Improvise eight bars over the two II-V-Is; at each change, land on a chord tone. Play at least 24 notes.

l511.title: Notes on the 6th and 5th strings
l511.objective: Find the natural notes on the 6th and 5th strings, up to fret 12.
l511.s1: "If you know where the notes are on the 6th and 5th strings, you know where any chord is."
l511.s2: On the 6th: open E, F on 1, G on 3, A on 5, B on 7, C on 8, D on 10 and E on 12.
l511.s3: On the 5th: open A, B on 2, C on 3, D on 5, E on 7, F on 8, G on 10 and A on 12.
l511.s4: "Between B and C, and between E and F, there is only one fret."
l511.c1b: The natural notes up to fret 12. Listen.
l511.q1: Which note is on fret 5 of the 6th string?
l511.tap: Press the natural notes of the 6th string on the fretboard.
l511.play6: Play the natural notes of the 6th string, from low to high.
l511.play5: Play the natural notes of the 5th string, from low to high.

l512.title: Octaves
l512.objective: Find the octave of a note: from the 6th to the 4th string and from the 5th to the 3rd, two frets up.
l512.s1: "The same note, higher: that is an octave."
l512.s2: From the 6th string: skip two strings and move up two frets.
l512.s3: From the 5th string: the same, up to the 3rd.
l512.s4: "With octaves you find any note without counting frets."
l512.c1b: A and C, with their octave on the 4th. Listen to the click.
l512.c2b: C and D, with their octave on the 3rd. Listen to the click.
l512.q1: Where is the octave of a note on the 6th string?
l512.q1o1: Two strings higher and two frets up
l512.q1o2: On the next string, same fret
l512.q1o3: On the same string, seven frets up
l512.tap: Press two notes and their octaves on the fretboard.
l512.play: Play each note and its octave, in time.

l513.title: The CAGED system
l513.objective: Play C major in three CAGED shapes: the open C shape, the A shape at fret 3 and the E shape at fret 8.
l513.s1: "Five open shapes: C, A, G, E and D. They link up all over the neck."
l513.s2: The C shape is the open C you already know.
l513.s3: The A shape, barred at fret 3; the E shape, barred at fret 8.
l513.s4: "One chord, three places: pick the one closest to the melody."
l513.c1b: Open C, note by note. Listen.
l513.c2b: C at fret 3 and at fret 8. Listen.
l513.q1o1: The five open shapes (C, A, G, E and D) repeating along the neck
l513.play: Play C major in the three shapes, note by note.
l513.timed: Play the three shapes of C in time.

l514.title: One chord all over the neck
l514.objective: Play A minor in three places: open, barred at fret 5 and with the A shape at fret 12.
l514.s1: "A minor does not live only in first position."
l514.s3: Barred at fret 5 (E shape) and at fret 12 (A shape).
l514.s4: "Choosing the place is choosing the colour."
l514.c2b: Am at fret 5 and at fret 12. Listen.
l514.q1: How many times can you play the same chord on the neck?
l514.q1o3: In several shapes, up to fret 12 and beyond
l514.play: Play A minor in the three places, in time.

l521.title: Triads on the top strings
l521.objective: Play the C, F and G triads on strings 3, 2 and 1.
l521.s1: "Three notes are enough for a chord."
l521.s2: Root, third and fifth, on the three high strings.
l521.s3: C, F, G and C, barely moving your hand.
l521.s4: "Small triads leave room for the bass and the band."
l521.c1b: C, F, G and C on strings 3, 2 and 1. Listen to the click.
l521.q1o1: Three notes: root, third and fifth
l521.play: Play the C, F, G and C triads, in time.

l522.title: Triads on the 4th, 3rd and 2nd strings
l522.objective: Play C, F, G and C on strings 4, 3 and 2, in different inversions.
l522.s1: "The same chord with another note on the bottom sounds different."
l522.s2: If the root is on the bottom, it is root position.
l522.s3: If the third is, first inversion; if the fifth is, second.
l522.s4: "Inversions keep the chords close to each other."
l522.c1b: C, F, G and C. Listen to the click.
l522.c2b: The triads from the last lesson. Compare.
l522.q1o2: Which note is on the bottom
l522.play: Play the triads on strings 4, 3 and 2, in time.

l523.title: C with E in the bass (C/E)
l523.objective: Fret C with E in the bass (C/E), make every note ring clean and strum it in time.
l523.s1: "A new chord for the album: C with E in the bass (C/E)."
l523.s2: Like open C, but the 6th string rings open: E on the bottom. Finger 3 on fret 3 of the 5th string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 4th and finger 1 on fret 1 of the 2nd.
l523.s3: Play string by string: if one doesn't ring, adjust that finger.
l523.s4: "And now with p-i-m-i, like in level 1."
l523.c1t: How to fret C with E in the bass (C/E)
l523.c1b: Like open C, but the 6th string rings open: E on the bottom. Finger 3 on fret 3 of the 5th string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 4th and finger 1 on fret 1 of the 2nd. Listen to its notes one at a time.
l523.c2b: The slash tells you the bass note: C/E is C with E on the bottom, the first inversion.
l523.tap: Press the notes of C with E in the bass (C/E) on the fretboard.
l523.arp: Fret C with E in the bass (C/E) and play string by string, from low to high.
l523.strum: Strum C with E in the bass (C/E) downward with your thumb, in quarter notes, in time.

l524.title: Voice leading
l524.objective: Play C, G/B, Am and G with the bass stepping down, and fret G/B.
l524.s2: The bass steps down: C, B, A, G.
l524.s3: G/B: finger 1 on fret 2 of the 5th string, fingers 3 and 4 on fret 3 of the 2nd and 1st; the 4th and 3rd open.
l524.s4: "If the notes move a little, the changes sound smooth."
l524.c2b: Your thumb follows the bass line. Listen.
l524.q1: What does the bass do in C, G/B, Am and G?
l524.q1o1: It steps down: C, B, A, G
l524.q1o2: It jumps from root to root
l524.strum: Strum C, G/B, Am and G in quarter notes, in time.
l524.pimi: Play C, G/B, Am and G in p-i-m-i, in time.
l524.tap: Press the notes of G/B on the fretboard.

l525.title: Walking basses
l525.objective: Connect G, D/F#, Em and C with a walking bass, and fret D/F#.
l525.s2: D/F#: finger 1 on fret 2 of the 6th string, finger 2 on fret 2 of the 3rd, finger 3 on fret 2 of the 1st and finger 4 on fret 3 of the 2nd; the 5th muted.
l525.s3: The bass steps down: G, F#, E, and arrives on C.
l525.s4: "Passing notes lead from one chord to the next."
l525.c2b: The same chords with the thumb on the bass. Listen.
l525.strum: Strum G, D/F#, Em and C in quarter notes, in time.
l525.pimi: Play G, D/F#, Em and C in p-i-m-i, in time.
l525.tap: Press the notes of D/F# on the fretboard.
l525.walk: Play the walking bass with your thumb, in time.

l531.title: Melody on top
l531.objective: Play an original melody on the high strings over C, Am, F and G.
l531.s1: "In chord-melody, the guitar sings and accompanies at the same time."
l531.s2: First, the melody alone, on the 1st and 2nd strings.
l531.s3: Every bar starts on a chord tone.
l531.s4: "If the melody sounds clear alone, then you add the rest."
l531.c1b: Four bars on the high strings. Listen to the click.
l531.c2b: C, Am, F and G. Listen.
l531.q1: In chord-melody, where does the melody go?
l531.q1o1: On top, on the high strings
l531.play: Play the melody alone, in time.

l532.title: The bass underneath
l532.objective: Play the melody with each chord's bass on beat 1: thumb below, fingers above.
l532.s1: "Now the thumb gives the melody a floor."
l532.s2: On beat 1 of every bar, the chord's bass with the thumb.
l532.s3: On beats 2, 3 and 4, the melody with i and m.
l532.s4: "The app hears one note at a time: that is why the bass goes alone on 1."
l532.c1b: The bass on 1 and the melody after. Listen to the click.
l532.c2b: Thumb on the low strings; i, m and a on the high ones.
l532.q1: If the app hears one note at a time, how do you play bass and melody?
l532.q1o2: The bass on 1 and the melody on the other beats
l532.play: Play the melody with the bass on 1, in time.

l533.title: The chord on the strong beat
l533.objective: Play the full chord on beat 1 of every bar and, separately, the melody with the bass.
l533.s1: "On the strong beat, the whole chord rings."
l533.s2: One stroke on 1 and the chord keeps ringing.
l533.s3: Then, the melody with the bass, like in the last lesson.
l533.s4: "When you play alone, put both together: chord on 1 and melody on top."
l533.c1b: C, Am, F and G, one stroke per bar. Listen to the click.
l533.c2b: The melody with the bass. Listen.
l533.q1: On which beat does the full chord ring?
l533.strum: Strum C, Am, F and G with one stroke on beat 1 of each bar.
l533.play: Play the melody with the bass on 1, in time.

l534.title: Fills
l534.objective: Add eighth-note fills between the long notes of the melody.
l534.s1: "When the melody rests, the guitar can comment."
l534.s2: After each long note, two eighth notes that lead to the next one.
l534.s3: Chord or scale notes, never louder than the melody.
l534.s4: "A fill is a bridge, not another melody."
l534.c1b: The melody with eighth notes between the long notes. Listen to the click.
l534.q1o1: Between the long notes of the melody
l534.q1o3: At the start of the bar
l534.play: Play the melody with the fills, in time.

l535.title: An 8-bar arrangement
l535.objective: Play an 8-bar chord-melody arrangement, with the bass on 1 and the melody on top.
l535.s2: The first four bars, like in "The bass underneath".
l535.s3: The other four go back to C through G/B.
l535.s4: "Play it slowly until your thumb and fingers stop thinking."
l535.c1b: Bass on 1 and melody on top. Listen to the click.
l535.c2b: The second phrase, back to C. Listen to the click.
l535.strum: Strum the chords of the arrangement in quarter notes: C, Am, F, G, C, G/B, F and C.

l541.title: Harmonics
l541.objective: Play the natural harmonics at fret 12 on all six strings.
l541.s1: "A bell-like sound, without pressing the string."
l541.s2: Rest your finger lightly right over fret 12, on the metal, without pressing.
l541.s3: Pluck and lift the finger right away: the note keeps ringing.
l541.s4: "They sound an octave above the open string."
l541.c1b: At fret 12, from the 6th string to the 1st. Listen.
l541.c2b: Right over fret 12, not between the frets.
l541.q1: How do you play a natural harmonic?
l541.q1o1: Resting your finger lightly over fret 12, without pressing
l541.q1o3: With the nail over the sound hole
l541.play: Play the harmonics at fret 12, from the 6th string to the 1st.

l542.title: Pizzicato
l542.objective: Play the bass in pizzicato: short notes muted with the edge of the right hand.
l542.s1: "A dry sound, like a plucked double bass."
l542.s2: Rest the edge of your right hand on the strings, near the bridge.
l542.s3: Pluck with the thumb: the note sounds short and muted.
l542.s4: "If it sounds dead, move your hand a little toward the bridge."
l542.c1b: Am, Dm, E7 and Am. Listen to the click.
l542.c2b: The edge of the hand barely touches the strings over the bridge.
l542.q1: What mutes the strings in pizzicato?
l542.q1o2: The edge of the right hand, near the bridge
l542.play: Play the bass in pizzicato, in time.

l543.title: Tambora
l543.objective: Play the tambora: strike the strings near the bridge with the side of the thumb, in half notes.
l543.s1: "The nylon guitar is also a drum."
l543.s2: Fret the chord and strike the strings near the bridge with the side of your thumb.
l543.s3: A quick hit and release: the chord sounds like a drumhead.
l543.s4: "It is the sound of zamba and chacarera when the guitar plays alone."
l543.c1b: Em and Am, two strikes per bar. Listen to the click.
l543.c2b: With the side of the thumb, near the bridge.
l543.q1: How do you play the tambora?
l543.q1o1: Striking the strings near the bridge with the side of the thumb
l543.q1o2: Strumming up with the index finger
l543.strum: Play the tambora on Em and Am, two strikes per bar, in time.

l544.title: The i-m-a rasgueo
l544.objective: Play the continuous rasgueo with a, m and i over the Andalusian cadence: Am, G, F and E.
l544.s1: "Three fingers, one after another: it sounds like a drum roll."
l544.s2: Close your hand and flick the fingers down: first a, then m, then i.
l544.s3: Three strokes in a row and a breath, twice per bar.
l544.c1b: Am, G, F and E with the continuous rasgueo, at 50. Listen to the click.
l544.q1: Which fingers play the continuous rasgueo?
l544.q1o1: a, m and i, one after another, downward
l544.strum: Play the continuous rasgueo on Am, G, F and E, in time.

l545.title: Nylon-string vibrato
l545.objective: Play vibrato by moving your hand along the string, on the long notes of a melody.
l545.s1: "On the nylon guitar, vibrato does not bend the string: it rocks it."
l545.s2: Press the note and move your hand toward the bridge and toward the nut, without letting go.
l545.s3: It is a narrow, even vibrato that makes the long note sing.
l545.s4: "Use it on long notes, not on all of them."
l545.c1b: Long notes to sing with vibrato. Listen.
l545.c2b: The finger stays put; the whole hand moves along the string.
l545.q1: How does the hand move in nylon-string vibrato?
l545.q1o2: Along the string, toward the bridge and the nut
l545.vib: Play vibrato on fret 5 of the 2nd string for 4 seconds.
l545.vib2: Play vibrato on fret 5 of the 1st string for 5 seconds.
l545.play: Play the melody with vibrato on the long notes, in time.

l551.title: The Dorian mode
l551.objective: Play A Dorian and improvise with it over Am7 and D7.
l551.s2: A Dorian is A natural minor with F raised: F#.
l551.s3: Over Am7 and D7, that major sixth is what you hear.
l551.s4: "Dorian is the minor of funk, jazz and a lot of Latin music."
l551.c1b: A, B, C, D, E, F#, G and A. Listen.
l551.c2b: Am7 and D7. Listen before you play.
l551.q1: Which note sets Dorian apart from natural minor?
l551.q1o1: The major sixth (F# in A Dorian)
l551.play: Play A Dorian, note by note.
l551.improv: Improvise with A Dorian over Am7 and D7; at each change, land on a chord tone. Play at least 16 notes.

l552.title: The Mixolydian mode
l552.objective: Play A Mixolydian and improvise with it over A and G.
l552.s2: A Mixolydian is A major with the seventh lowered: G.
l552.s3: Over A and G, that G is in charge.
l552.s4: "It is the major of rock, folk and many popular songs."
l552.c1b: A, B, C#, D, E, F#, G and A. Listen.
l552.c2b: A and G. Listen before you play.
l552.q1: Which note sets Mixolydian apart from the major scale?
l552.q1o2: The minor seventh (G in A Mixolydian)
l552.play: Play A Mixolydian, note by note.
l552.improv: Improvise with A Mixolydian over A and G; at each change, land on a chord tone. Play at least 16 notes.

l553.title: The Phrygian mode
l553.objective: Play E Phrygian and improvise with it over Em and F.
l553.s1: "The darkest mode: it sounds like flamenco."
l553.s2: E Phrygian is the notes of C major from E: E, F, G, A, B, C, D.
l553.s3: The F, a half step above the root, gives it its tension.
l553.s4: "Em and F, back and forth: that is all it needs."
l553.c1b: E, F, G, A, B, C, D and E. Listen.
l553.c2b: Em and F. Listen before you play.
l553.q1: Which note gives Phrygian its colour?
l553.q1o3: The minor second (F in E Phrygian)
l553.play: Play E Phrygian, note by note.
l553.improv: Improvise with E Phrygian over Em and F; at each change, land on a chord tone. Play at least 16 notes.

l554.title: Choosing the mode
l554.objective: Recognize by ear which mode a backing asks for and improvise with the right one.
l554.s1: "The backing tells you which mode to use."
l554.s2: Minor with D7: Dorian. Major with the seventh lowered: Mixolydian.
l554.s3: Minor with the chord a half step up (Em and F): Phrygian.
l554.s4: "Listen to two rounds before you play your first note."
l554.c1b: Listen: which mode does it ask for?
l554.c2b: Listen: which mode does it ask for?
l554.ear: Listen to the backing. Which mode does it ask for?
l554.ear2: Listen to this other backing. Which mode does it ask for?
l554.improv: Improvise with the mode the Am7–D7 backing asks for; at each change, land on a chord tone. Play at least 16 notes.

l561.title: Choosing the song
l561.objective: Get to know the final project song and play its accompaniment: Am, F, C, G, Am, F, E7 and Am.
l561.s1: "The project is here: your arrangement, with the band."
l561.s2: The song is an original ballad in A minor, eight bars long.
l561.s3: First, the accompaniment with the ballad pattern.
l561.s4: "Always choose something you can play calmly: the arrangement adds difficulty."
l561.c1b: Eight bars with the ballad pattern. Listen.
l561.c2b: Am, F, C, G, Am, F, E7 and Am, in quarter notes.
l561.q1: What should you check first when choosing the project song?
l561.q1o1: That it uses chords and techniques you already play comfortably
l561.q1o2: That it is the hardest one
l561.q1o3: That it has lots of new chords
l561.strum: Play the project accompaniment with the ballad pattern, in time.

l562.title: The arrangement
l562.objective: Play the project chord-melody arrangement: bass on 1 and the melody on top.
l562.s1: "Now one guitar plays the whole song."
l562.s2: On beat 1 of each bar, the chord's bass with the thumb.
l562.s3: On the other beats, the melody on the high strings.
l562.s4: "If a change is hard, practise just those two bars."
l562.c1b: Bass and melody. Listen to the click.
l562.c2b: The second half, ending on Am. Listen to the click.
l562.q1: In your arrangement, what does the thumb play on 1?
l562.play: Play the project arrangement, slowly and in time.

l563.title: With the band
l563.objective: Play the arrangement in time and an 8-bar solo with the A minor pentatonic over the song.
l563.s1: "The band comes in: now you cannot stop."
l563.s2: First the arrangement, in time with the band.
l563.s3: Then an eight-bar solo, landing on a chord tone at each change.
l563.s4: "If you get lost, come back in on beat 1 of the next bar."
l563.c1b: The song with the ballad pattern. Listen.
l563.solo: Play an 8-bar solo with the A minor pentatonic; at each change, land on a chord tone. Play at least 16 notes.

l564.title: The performance
l564.objective: Play the whole project at 80: strummed intro, the arrangement and the solo.
l564.s2: Intro: the eight bars with the ballad pattern.
l564.s3: Then the arrangement, and to finish, the solo.
l564.s4: "Breathe before you start and do not stop for a mistake."
l564.c2b: The band that plays with you. Listen.
l564.q1: Before performing, what should you do?
l564.q1o1: Play it all the way through at a comfortable tempo, without stopping
l564.q1o2: Push the tempo to the max
l564.intro: Play the intro with the ballad pattern, at 80.
l564.solo: Finish with an 8-bar solo with the A minor pentatonic. Play at least 16 notes.

cp5.intro: Your final project: the accompaniment, the chord-melody arrangement and a solo, with the band.
cp5.ear: Listen to the backing. Which mode does it ask for?
cp5.intro2: Play the project accompaniment with the ballad pattern, in time.
cp5.arrangement: Play your arrangement: bass on 1 and the melody on top, in time.
cp5.solo: Play an 8-bar solo with the A minor pentatonic; at each change, land on a chord tone. Play at least 20 notes.

cp3.intro: Show what you learned in level 3: E- and A-shape barre chords, the 12-bar blues and a solo with slurs.
cp3.ear: Listen to the chord. Is it a triad or does it have a seventh?
cp3.barres: Strum the barre chord progression (B♭, Gm, Cm, F7, F, F#m, Bm7, E7), in time.
cp3.blues: Strum the 12-bar blues in E, in time.
cp3.solo: Play the phrase with slurs, note by note.

onboarding.welcomeBody: Short lessons, cartoons and exercises with or without your guitar. 15 minutes a day.
onboarding.hasBass: Do you have an electric guitar?

songbook.intro: Original riffs and melodies to play by genre, with a backing track. They unlock with the modules where you learn what they use.
songbook.playPrompt: Play it on your guitar, in time with the metronome.
songbook.chordsHint: One chord per bar. In the example they play in the background; your guitar plays the melody or riff.

tip.octave: The same note is two strings up and two frets along: that's its octave. If the jump goes past the 3rd and 2nd strings (G and B), it's three frets.

onboarding.hasBass: Do you have a classical guitar?
